 {'content': "- Lift the horse's foot - Make sure to raise the horse's hoof in a way that is comfortable and natural, and make sure the horse is aware of your presence beforehand, so it is not startled. Put your hand on the horse's leg, and run your hand down until you reach the tendon above the ankle. When the horse feels this, it will shift its weight to the other three legs. Once you have the foot raised, try resting it between your knees, with the sole facing up toward you.

- Remove the existing shoe - Use a clinch cutter to straighten the nails holding the old shoe on, then use a pair of metal pull-offs to remove the shoe from the hoof. This can also be done with a flat screwdriver. Wiggle the tool in a rocking motion until it is loose enough to pull off by hand.

- Clean the hoof - Make sure to clean away any dirt and debris to prevent it from being trapped between the hoof and the new shoe. Use a hoof pick to remove dirt or manure, using downward strokes from heel to toe. Follow up with a wire brush to remove any remaining debris. Be careful of the fleshy area here because it is very sensitive.

- Remove the excess hoof - Use a hoof knife to remove the excess flaky part of the bottom of the hoof. The outer layer will be hard and dark, and once cut, the hoof underneath will be softer and whiter, similar to a human's toenail. Make sure not to cut too deep, and not to cut yourself.

- Trim excess hoof wall - The hoof wall is the edge of the hoof. It should only extend about 3 inches from the hairline of the hoof. If it is longer than this, trim it back and make sure to cut it straight and level so it will sit flush with the ground when standing.

- Use a rasp for leveling - This is the last step before applying a new shoe. Use a rasp and gently file any uneven areas so that the hoof is smooth and level. prompt: What are some techniques i can use when negotiating. This will be concerning my pay.
messages:
[{'content': 'What are some techniques i can use when negotiating. This will be concerning my pay.', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': "Here are five tips to use when negotiating your pay. 

1. Know your worth.
Before entering negotiations regarding your pay, you must know what you are worth. Knowing what you are worth to a company will give you a base for negotiations. It can be tough to see what you are worth to your company, but luckily, you can use sites like glassdoor.com and payscale.com to get a better idea of what people in similar roles and companies to you do earn. This knowledge will mean you can confidently suggest a number in line with the market rate. Offering a rate identical to others in your field will allow you to have confidence that the company will not be able to find someone better without at least paying an equal rate. Hiring new staff is often tedious and not cost-effective, so forcing your employer into this decision can work in your favor. 

2. Use good timing. 
Timing is everything in negotiations, which is never more true than in salary negotiations. Utilizing good timing can be the difference between a successful salary negotiation and an awkward conversation with your boss. Try to initiate salary negotiations while the company is doing well and you are being seen to impact that success substantially. A salesman who isn't hitting targets regularly would be ill-advised to open negotiations regarding salary. It may be that they can get a higher wage but unlikely to be sufficient if they don't have the data to back up their claimed performances. If you've just completed a profitable project and been a key player, it's probably a great time to strike while the iron is hot and ask for a pay rise. 

3. Be realistic.
It is necessary to know your worth and understand your value to a company, but remaining realistic is also pivotal. If you aim for the stars and ask for 50% more than you are worth, you can expect your employer to grow frustrated and unsympathetic to your request. The better tactic is to have a number in mind you would like, then add a small % to it so that you can work down to your ideal number. This will allow your employer some wiggle room to negotiate and feel they are not being played. It is essential to back your realistic request up with why you deserve it and what others are getting. 

4. Don't ask too often. 
As stated above, alienating and frustrating your employer is not a good idea. If you do this, you risk no negotiations and just a simple no. This will leave you in no better position than you were before. That is precisely why it is essential not to ask too frequently for a pay rise. Think of a similar situation in the car when a child asks the parents are we there yet over and over. The parents become frustrated and eventually will stop answering. The same will happen with your employer. They will revert to a standard no answer if you continuously ask for something. Instead, be sure to research what you are worth and strike while the iron is hot, as we described in point 2. 

5. Don't be afraid to ask. 
It seems silly to put this point straight after point 4. However, the fact is valid and should be discussed. While asking too often is not advised, not asking at all will probably get you nowhere. While this can't be said for all companies, most are reluctant to hand out pay raises regularly and will wait until they are asked or forced. That's why it is crucial that if you feel you deserve a pay rise and the circumstances dictate one, you stand up for yourself and ask. The worst thing they can say is no. If you don't think you deserve a pay raise, that's fine. Don't ask till you do. But if you have been stuck at the same rate for years and are integral to our company's operations, then speak up and ask for your worth. 
", 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: Give me 7 tips for writing an awesome CV.
messages:
[{'content': 'Give me 7 tips for writing an awesome CV.', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': 'Of course. Below, I have written seven tips for writing a standout CV.

1. Start strong. 
Start your CV by listing your best achievements to date. Highlight your skills and experience, and just champion yourself. The goal of a CV is to convince a potential employer you are the right fit for them, so don't be shy and tell them exactly why your skills and experience will assist their company. If you don't get this bit right, it is unlikely recruiters will get much further into your CV. 

2. Emphasize past results rather than responsibilities. 
When detailing your work history, try to avoid discussing what you were responsible for and instead highlight your actual results. It is far more meaningful for someone to see results rather than try to infer what you have achieved through roles and responsibilities. It sounds better to say, "I ensured the completion of 5 major projects within my time at the company," rather than, "In my role, I was responsible for major projects."

3. Customise. 
One CV does not fit all jobs. Try to tailor your CV to the job you are applying for, and bring to the fore the experiences that suit the role and company you are applying to. Research the company to understand who they are, then tailor your CV to match its ethos and culture.

4. Highlight growth and change. 
Change is good, and growth is even better. If you have been promoted or changed roles at a previous company, mention that. Recruiters will take that as you are versatile and willing to learn. This will give them affirmation from the actions of your previous employer that you were both competent and proactive. 

5. Demonstrate your network. 
Showcase that if you have a large network and are well connected. Employers will see that as an opportunity to hire you and get the added bonus of your well-established network as a resource. If you are hired, they get two for the price of one. 

6. Show industry insight. 
It doesn't hurt to give a small opinion if you are applying to an industry that's currently topical or experiencing changes. Doing this shows you are current, in the know, and committed to your career in this industry. You don't have to give an opinion. You could forecast a change you foresee and mention how you see this impacting a role. 

7. Use powerful words. 
A CV is extremely important in grabbing a recruiter's attention. Using powerful words like implemented and adaptable will help you stand out from the crowd and keep your CV in the prospects' file. Consider the difference in the sentences "I am willing to change" and "I am very adaptable" one seems weak, and one seems far stronger. You can research topical power words online or use the thesaurus feature in Microsoft word to make your language stand out. ', 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: Give me a list of things to consider when trying to identify my target audience. I own a tech company and am trying to get more brand awareness.
messages:
[{'content': 'Give me a list of things to consider when trying to identify my target audience. I own a tech company and am trying to get more brand awareness.', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': "Here are eight things to consider when identifying your target audience. 

1. Analyze current customers.
If you are in a position where you have existing customers, then a good first step is to identify traits and characteristics among them. Think about the demographic they belong to and why they may be purchasing products or services from you already. You may already have data regarding your current customer's ages, locations, and vocations. These are all valuable metrics to track and interpret when defining your target audience. 

2. Market research.
Conducting market research is a valuable process. By conducting market research, you can identify areas in which you may be able to grow an audience or a blind spot where your services could be of real value. Looking into your competitors can provide great insights into what works and doesn't and where services like yours perform well. Knowing what others offer gives you an advantage when creating a unique selling point that sets you apart. 

3. Industry trends. 
Keeping your finger on the pulse and identifying what changes are occurring within your industry allows you to tailor content and services in a way that provides real value. This leads on from market research slightly and is another way of ensuring you stay informed concerning your customers' expectations and desires. This will allow you to provide them with a constant value.  

4. Distinguish benefits from features. 
Benefits and features are fundamentally different things. It is important to clarify this to your target audience. It is excellent that you have a feature or product that can help them in some way, but it's even better if you can explain the practical benefit of the feature. Take, for example, a product that improves productivity. Emphasizing productivity improvement and what that means is more important than highlighting the actual feature that does the work. People are more interested in what you will enable them to do rather than how you will do it. 

5. Spy on your competition. 
Just as important as your customers are your competitors. Keep an eye on what they are doing and the content they are producing. What could be working for them, and what could you do to improve what they have? This is an easy way to gain inspiration and see what's not being offered. This will allow you to fill in the gaps and potentially convert customers to you and your services. If your competition produces content about something you are not, this may mean they have researched and identified a weak spot. Now you can do your own research and improve on what they have done. 

6. Who isn't your target audience?
Knowing who your target audience is made much easier if you can identify exactly who it isn't. Who won't benefit from what you are offering or take an interest in what you are saying? By analyzing these questions, you can reduce your audience to specifics and tailor your services to those likely to benefit from and purchase them. Doing this will give you more time to concentrate on those that matter. 

7. Be objective. 
Making assumptions can lead to alienating some of your customer base. This can be avoided by posting content that leads by facts more than anything else. By being objective, you show your customers you can be trusted and only care about black and white. This should help to foster a sense of trust in you and your products. 

8. Go niche. 
It may seem like going to a niche would limit your customers, and while that may be true to an extent, you shouldn't underestimate how many people are in the world. And also how being a leading figure in a super niche topic can grow your audience quickly and lead you to be the go-to person in said niche. Also, it is worth remembering that while your niche may mean fewer customers or audiences, it also means less competition. 
", 'role': 'assistant'}]

 {'content': "The world is full of amazing travel destinations, so it's understandably challenging to choose the perfect place to go. Here is a list of the best places to visit if you don't want a beach vacation and don't like big cities:

1. Glacier National Park
Glacier National Park is one of the most striking parks in North America. Snow-capped peaks and crystal-blue lakes, over 700 miles of hiking trails, and plenty of camping areas make this a great option for an adventurous holiday. There is a lot to do all year. In the winter, you can go snowshoeing and skiing, and in the summer, you can swim in Lake McDonald or go whitewater rafting on the Flathead River. There are also beautiful scenic drives if you prefer to go the comfortable route.

2. The Swiss Alps
The Swiss Alps are world-famous for their snow-covered mountains and cute little towns. If you visit in the winter, you will get some world-class skiing in St. Moritz or Zermatt. If you go in the summer, you can hike through the Swiss National Park or attend some festivals in Montreux. Don't forget to visit the Jungfrau Region to see the most idyllic mountain villages like Grindelwald and Mürren.

3. Costa Rica
Costa Rica offers travelers everything from volcanic mountains and rainforests to waterfalls and a stunning shoreline. You can hike along Arenal Volcano, try to spot exotic wildlife like river turtles, otters, and howler monkeys in Tortuguero National Park, swim next to some of the country's waterfalls, or zip line through rainforests. Just make sure you visit between mid-December and April, when Costa Rica has its dry season.

4. South Island, New Zealand
New Zealand's South Island offers amazing landscapes, beautiful mountains, and impressive fjords. From hiking trails to boat trips, you have limitless possibilities. Visit the Mount John Observatory for some peaceful stargazing at night, or go for the adrenaline experience in Queenstown for some bungee jumping. Make sure to visit a few wineries and indulge in winetasting if you visit the Marlborough region and stop by the two most accessible glaciers, Franz Josef and Fox Glacier, on the west coast.

5. Tasmania
Tasmania is Australia's island in the south, about 150 miles from the mainland. It has an abundance of wildlife like Tasmanian devils, penguins, and kangaroos, impressive scenery, and 19 national parks to explore. Visit Hobart and Launceston for some acclaimed art and gastronomy experiences, or give their wine trails a try to taste some pinot noir and sparkling options.", 'role': 'assistant'}]

messages:

 {'content': "President Dwight D. Eisenhower created the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) by signing the National Aeronautics and Space Act on July 29, 1958. Assets and research programs previously administrated by the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) were transferred to NASA as part of the act.

The creation of NASA was a response to the USSR's launch of a series of Sputnik satellites. The USSR launched the first Sputnik satellite on October 4, 1957. This launch is generally recognized as the start of the Space Age. It also officially began the Space Race between the USSR and the United States of America.

The United States of America initially saw NASA and the Space Race as a matter of national security. Whoever controlled space would have the high ground in the event of a conflict. At the time, the USSR and USA were locked in the Cold War, a political and ideological rivalry between the two superpowers.

NASA was given the task of developing the space capabilities of the United States, including creating the capacity to launch living organisms and hardware into space. Early efforts to launch organisms into space included launching two monkeys named Able and Baker on a suborbital flight on May 28, 1959. Both monkeys survived, though Able died two years later and Baker spent most of her life on display after the flight. NASA's Mercury Program also launched chimpanzees on test flights before sending astronauts.

During the 1960s and 1970s, NASA conducted the Mercury, Gemini, Apollo, and Skylab programs, which taught many valuable lessons about conducting space missions that it still uses. Apollo sent crews to the Moon for the first time during the late 1960s and early 1970s.

While the Cold War ended with the collapse of the USSR, NASA continues to conduct scientific research in space and conduct its crewed space programs. 2. Watch what you eat and drink - Don't have heavy or large meals within a couple of hours of going to bed, and don't go to bed either hungry or stuffed with food. Also, nicotine, caffeine, and alcohol can all affect sleep, so keep an eye on those.

5. Add physical activity to your daily routine - Avoid being active too close to bedtime, but making sure you get regular physical activity can help promote good sleep. Also, spending time outside is helpful.

 {'content': "Sound is created when an object vibrates, causing air molecules to move and bump into each other, which causes vibrations. This chain reaction of bumping molecules is what we call a sound wave.

If the vibrations are moving at a certain speed, you can hear it, but you cannot hear the sound of something slow such as your hand passing slowly through the air. The slowest vibration you can hear is 20 vibrations per second which is a low pitch sound, and the fastest you can hear is 20,000 vibrations per second which is a high pitch sound. The number of vibrations per second is what we call the object's frequency which is measured in Hertz.

The pitch of a sound depends on the vibrating object's weight. The more mass, the slower it vibrates, which means a lower pitch, and the less mass, the faster it vibrates, which means a higher pitch. prompt: What are some vet-approved homemade dog food recipes?
messages:
[{'content': 'What are some vet-approved homemade dog food recipes?', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': "Below is a general starting point for a recipe adapted from veterinarian Greg Martinez by The Wildest's Claudia Kaawczynska. She points out that this slow-cooker-made recipe is higher in protein, with about 50% dry matter, and lower in fat, with about 10% dry matter than you'd find in most recipes. She adds that, since every pet has very specific needs, you should only use this recipe as a starting point, then talk things over with your pet's doctor for more specifics suited to them. 

The ingredients you will need are: 

* 3/4ths minimum to 1 pound maximum of cubed, skinless, boneless chicken breasts or thighs. (Substitute with lean beef, turkey, or fish if necessary or preferred)

* 1 ounce minimum to 3 ounces maximum of preferably chicken liver, hearts, or gizzards. Other animal livers are acceptable.

* If this meal accounts for more than 10% of a dog's daily diet, include 1 tablespoon of bone meal (or 1,500 mg) per pound of meat

* 1 to 2 whole eggs for a healthy source of fat 

* 8 ounces of brown or white rice

* 16 ounces of green beans

* Water

Take your slow cooker and add in the diced chicken, the chicken liver, gizzards, and hearts, along with the eggs. You will then add the bone meal, rice, and green beans. Denser ingredients should be at the bottom, with the lightest ingredients on top. Since the amount of water you'll need to use depends on how long you choose to cook the ingredients and how big your slow cooker is, there isn't a specific amount you need to add. Try to fill the cooker to about two-thirds of the way full, but not less than halfway, and if possible, use a six-or-seven quart cooker. When you add in the water, you should try to submerge the ingredients without fully covering them. Then, stir the contents.

Put on the lid and set the temperature to low. Leave your crockpot on for around 4 to 8 hours, only as long as needed for the chicken breasts to fall apart. prompt: What are 6 things to consider when building a personal budget? Please list them out, and provide a detailed explanation of each.
messages:
[{'content': 'What are 6 things to consider when building a personal budget? Please list them out, and provide a detailed explanation of each. ', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': "Sure thing! To create your personal budget, follow these six steps. 

1. Calculate your net income. 
Start by creating your net income. Net income is the money you earn after all taxes and fees have been accounted for; it is the money that figuratively ends up in your pocket at the end of each month. This is important as the foundation of your budget. It determines how much you have available to allocate to your expense categories. A common mistake people make when calculating income is to use the gross total before taxes and pension contributions. This means they anticipate more income than they actually receive and thus leads to an inaccurate budget. To find your net income, you can look closely at some historic payslips or use one of the many online calculators. 

2. Track your spending.
The next step is to track and categorize your spending habits for 1-3 months. I would advise three months to ensure any quarterly payments are included; however, one month is enough to get a sense of spending habits in most areas. This is important as it will give you an idea of where your money goes each month and give you a solid base to create a monthly budget. To do this, you can write down each transaction you make throughout a period and assign it a category. Use an Excel spreadsheet to make things easier for you. Most banks will allow you to download a CSV file that includes all your transactions for a pre-determined period. Once downloaded, you can write a category next to each transaction. 

3. Set attainable goals.
The next thing you need to account for is the goals you have. Ensure that your goals are attainable and set a period for them also. Common goals are to pay down debt you have previously accrued or establish savings such as a three-month emergency fund. These goals should primarily be short-term and achievable within 1 to 3 years. It is ok to establish longer-term goals, but for your monthly budget, the short-term is what we are most interested in. Make sure these are motivating goals, as these will help to keep you on track when you want to disregard your budget. 

4. Make your plan. 
This is where you start to formulate a budget. You have your recorded transactions and your income. Look at your recorded expenses and determine for each category what a good budget would be for each month. For some of your fixed costs, this will be obvious. Your rent, for example, will not vary month on month. Your variable costs, such as eating out, may vary monthly, so set a middle ground you are comfortable with. You will need to make separate categories that consider your goals, for instance, a vacation category where you aim to save $100 monthly. All your budgeted expenses totaled should fall within your net income number. If it doesn't, you will have to cut back somewhere. 

5. Stick to your budget. 
Take great care to stick within your budget. Your budget guarantees reaching those goals and living within your means. Continue to track your spending to ensure you are remaining within budget. If you see certain categories are almost fully spent and it is only the 9th of the month, this should help you to stop spending in that category. If you overspend in one category, consider reducing spending in another to stay on track. Use your goals as motivation to stick with it.

6. Review regularly. 
A budget is only as good as when you do it, so maintain and update it as necessary. A pay raise at work will mean your budget can be adjusted to show more income and more capacity to save or spend. It's always good to review your budget at least quarterly, but the best budgets are updated monthly to account for the variables of life, such as birthdays, events, and other one-off occasions. It's unlikely that your December (Christmas) budget is the same as your budget for February. Use a forward-thinking approach to maintain and update your budget. There is no harm in reducing your budget in one month, so you can increase it in another so long as combined, they are within your income. ", 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: Write a blog post titled "Do Bluelight Glasses Actually Work?"
messages:
[{'content': 'Write a blog post titled "Do Bluelight Glasses Actually Work?"', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': "

Marketers of blue light glasses claim that their products block harmful blue light to reduce digital eye strain, which can cause headaches and eye discomfort. However, there isn't a lot of sound research to back these claims. It's also important to note that some brands are more effective at blocking blue light than others. 

For those that suffer from migraines and light sensitivity, a specific light-filtering (not just blue light) lens may be beneficial. For the majority of people that just want to reduce digital eye strain, blue light glasses may not do much. People are better off monitoring their screen time and following the 20-20-20 rule according to experts. This involves looking at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes. 

Where did the idea come from that we need to be blocking blue light you ask? The biggest source of blue light is from the sun, but when we say blue light, we're usually referring to artificial blue light from digital screens. In an evolving digital world, people are spending more and more time in front of screens. This is associated with some health problems like eye strain, headaches, and sleep disturbances.

Some scientists hypothesized the role of blue light in these issues.  An in vitro study (meaning in cells not in real humans) alluded to the fact that blue light harms ocular cells. A research study in mice illustrated that as exposure to blue light increased, instances of cataracts increased. Other recent research concluded that blue light glasses did not help mitigate the effects of screen exposure compared to a placebo. Research into this area is ongoing, but there is no undisputed answer at this point in time. 

There is slightly stronger research into the effects of blue light on melatonin. Some anecdotal evidence suggests that wearing blue light glasses before sleep may improve sleep quality. 

To summarize, if you are looking to reduce digital eye strain, blue light glasses should not be the sole solution. If you feel that they help, by all means, invest in a good pair from a reputable brand. The best ways to reduce eye strain though is to remain at arm's length from your screen, follow the 20-20-20 rule, and try and reduce your overall screen time. ", 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: Define the meaning of mythology. Tell me three stories from Greek or Roman times that are considered legends or folklore. Give me a short summary of each

 {'content': 'Mythology is taken from the Grecian words for mythos and logos, meaning the story of people through word or voice. They are often tales about culture and human emotions and conditions, passed down through generations and retold hundreds of thousands of times. Some mythologies are fables in that they teach lessons, while others are explanations to explain things like death, love, life, and the universe. 

Two of the most well-known cultures for mythologies are Greek and Roman. They often spoke of Gods, Goddesses, Titans, and Heroes. You’ve probably seen many of those cultures’ mythologies played out in modern books and movies. Hercules, for instance, is based on Grecian mythology, told, and retold, over centuries. 

Here are three more instances of Greek or Roman myths. 

•	The Three Fated Sisters of Life and Death

Clotho, Lachesis, and Atropos were three sisters, tasked with weaving the fates of both humans and gods. While Clotho spins the thread of life from someone’s birth, like an origin story, Lachesis is responsible for the continuation of the thread through life’s ups and downs. The latter measures the length of the thread to determine the longevity of the fated person. Finally, Atropos cuts the thread, foreseeing how someone will die. 

•	The Weaving Wars of Athena and Arachne 

Arachne was a weaver, and she could create elaborate quilts and tapestries from simple threads. Radiant in her confidence, she challenged Athena, the goddess of the arts, to a weaving contest, and the goddess accepted. However, where Athena wove a tapestry that portrayed her hard-fought battle with Poseidon, Arachne mocked Athena with a woven tapestry of Zeus (Athena’s father) up to his naughty antics. Athena took great offense, turning Arachne into a spider, cursed to hang forever in her woven webs. 

•	The Curse of the Bee’s Sting 

Humans have always taken a liking to honey, much to the chagrin of Bee, a hive queen in Rome. She journeyed to Mount Olympus, seeking counsel with Jupiter, to ask him to give her a stinger that would be so toxic that it would kill humans that stole her honey. Jupiter had a love for the human race, but he had made Bee a promise after tasting her delicious honey. The God King decided to teach her a lesson about wishing for the downfall of others.   8. Peppers: sweet and hot peppers are generally easier to grow than bell peppers. Jalapeno and purple beauty are two of the easiest varieties to grow.

3. Calculate expenses. This involves creating a budget, calculating fixed and variable expenses, working out quarterly estimated taxes, deciding on a savings plan, and buying insurance policies.

They can usually withstand temperatures of 1,000 degrees Celsius without degrading and some formulations can take much higher heat loads.

Some elements on the periodic table can be considered ceramic on their own. Pure carbon and silicon are among the more common elements that can be considered ceramic. Artificial ceramics are made by forming the item you want from clay or a conglomeration of specialty materials and then heating (firing) it until the material will no longer dissolve in water. Many ceramic items are also glazed on the surface so that water cannot soak into the material’s natural pores. 

Modern materials scientists have formulated specialty ceramics, but at their most basic, humans have been making artificial ceramics for at least 26,000 years. [{'content': 'Write an exaggerative, funny story about temptation where someone on a diet finds themselves at a buffet and tries their best not to grab themselves a plate.', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': 'The smell of fries, pizza, tiramisu, steak, and sushi seem like they would fill the air with aromas repulsing each other like oppositely-charged magnets, but Stu had been on a self-inflicted diet for months now and the buffet was calling his name. He only came as part of a mandatory business trip, and now he had to see his coworker’s plates piled higher than their chests with gooey cheese bites and crispy shrimp. The slot machines on The Strip failed to tempt Stu when his coworkers were gambling their money away in celebration of closing the new deal, but the honey-glaze on the bbq ribs had a different type of power.

As a courtesy, Stu had paid for a plate before sitting down because the anxiety to come if the buffet staff might suspect him of sneaking food without paying would be unbearable. So, there it was: a large, empty white plate sitting in front of him. The buffet ticket included a drink, but Stu refused that pleasure as well. Stu began rethinking his life decisions. He had been on this new diet for months and other diets for years with no rewards to show for any of it. The only thing he gained was a conversation topic everyone was tired of hearing about. Stu could no longer simply place the entire blame on food—there must be a different solution.

Stu had enough. The conversating coworkers around him fell silent as they noticed him pick up his plate and excuse himself from the table. No one could believe it. They watched him at the first buffet bar. Then, to the second. Stu stopped at every single station along the route and picked up at least one food item from the inviting warming platters. Stu’s eyes must have been piercing through the plexiglass sanitary guards as he drafted each piece of his bounty.

Returning to the table, Stu’s plate was so tall it obscured his eye line. His tablemates peered from either side of the food tower and saw Stu smiling for the first time in months—years, maybe. Stu proceeded to have the time of his life at the buffet and allowed that experience to renew him to forgo dieting altogether, beginning his search for a new path to a healthier lifestyle.', 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: Write a brief guide with tips on how best to "manage up" to senior leaders.

 {'content': 'Managing up to senior leaders and executive is a skill that most mid-level employees take years to master. It can be difficult to manage the personalities and unspoken factors that influence these interactions. Here are a few tips that can be of assistance: 

∙ Be clear and concise: structure your communication logically. For example, you could start by stating the issue or goal you want to discuss, then explain why it's important, and finally present your solution or recommendation. It's also important to avoid using jargon or acronyms that might make sense to you but are unfamiliar to a leader who isn't as "in the weeds" of the work. 

∙ Be prepared with the information you need to communicate: Think through what information your listener might need to understand your point of view, and then make sure you have that information ready. This can help you avoid being put on the spot or having to wing it. 

∙ Know your audience: Try to do some advanced research on who you'll be talking with and get an understanding of their perspective on the topic. What are their priorities? What are they looking to hear or discuss? With senior leaders, it's often helpful to understand their management style and how they like to receive information. Some leaders might like data and stats, while others want a more descriptive presentation. 

∙ Be proactive rather than reactive: Try to take the initiative to communicate, rather than waiting for a problem to arise or a question to be asked. Being proactive can also mean anticipating potential issues and addressing them before they become a problem. Try to get ahead of the game.

These tips can make an immediate impact towards being a more effective communicator. One more thing to keep in mind though: always seek feedback. Just because you considered the checklist above doesn't mean there isn't room for you to improve. Asking for feedback from your senior leaders can help you understand what's working well and where you can make adjustments. ', 'role': 'assistant'}]

messages:

How can they feel more relaxed about their physical state and not trigger a placebo effect to make them think there's something wrong with them?", 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': "Here is a list of three ways people can reduce their medical anxiety:
1) Work with a Primary Care Physician. By developing a relationship with a single doctor who can access all of your health records, you are gaining access to someone who can help ease any sense of paranoia you may be experiencing. Not only can they give you answers to possible problems you're having, but they are trained to help you through all sorts of concerns you have regarding your health and they will be able to refer you to a therapist if necessary. It's helpful to disclose that you are experiencing health anxiety so they can work with you on record keeping, tracking the actual state of your health, and avoiding costly and unnecessary screening tests.
2) Live a healthier lifestyle. If you are worried about your physical health, it may help to improve your lifestyle. When your body feels good, your mind does too. Try exercising, eating healthier, and drinking more water. There's also more that goes into a healthier lifestyle, like interaction. Stay active in your community, make new friends, try new hobbies, and go out of your comfort zone.
3) Regularly attend check-ups. Don't miss any check-ups, whether it be for a doctor, dentist, or another specialist. While you're at these check-ups, ask any questions you have about your health and share your concerns with them. They can help you feel better about any medical anxiety you have.
4) Meditate. Meditation is a way to feel your body and appreciate it, even when it doesn't feel perfectly comfortable. By meditating, you are practicing looking deeper within and experiencing what your body is feeling. You'll have a better understanding of your body and what's going on with it through meditation. Meditation is also relaxing and can help ease your feelings of anxiety. Along with that, meditation can help you to understand the signals your body is sending so that you can practice regular and effective self-care rather than rushing to a doctor's office to address every passing ache and pain.", 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: Dear computer-gods, please explain why some airplanes have wings that go straight across, some angle upwards, and some angle downwards? Why isn’t one style best?
messages:
[{'content': 'Dear computer-gods, please explain why some airplanes have wings that go straight across, some angle upwards, and some angle downwards? Why isn’t one style best?', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': 'The first thing you have to understand is that a positive dihedral (a wing that angles upward from the fuselage) creates roll stability – in other words, it will make the plane less inclined to roll to the left or right. The physics behind this so-called "dihedral effect" is complicated, but the basics are fairly easy to visualize; a positive dihedral moves the overall center of lift a little higher, placing it closer to – or sometimes above – the aircraft’s total center of mass. Effectively, with enough dihedral effect, the weight is hanging under the force that’s holding it up (as opposed to balancing on top).\xa0

As you might expect, this sort of stability is often beneficial. You don’t typically want your airliner or cargo plane to flip upside-down, after all. But there are reasons to angle the wing the other way.\xa0

Oftentimes, when the wing is mounted high, the center of mass is already far below the center of the lift. This can make some roll maneuvers excessively difficult. A negative dihedral angle (often called an anhedral) can reduce this roll resistance to more reasonable levels. Many military cargo aircraft, like the An-124 and C-5, are designed this way.

Some planes are built with a dihedral angle that intentionally reduces their roll stability. Though it sounds counterintuitive, fighter aircraft are most maneuverable if they are at least slightly aerodynamically unstable. The proper dihedral angle can help them hit the right balance between stability and instability.', 'role': 'assistant'}]

 {'content': 'Trash littered within a community is unpleasant and can be hard to prevent if the culprits are unknown. Here are some ways to prevent trash from being littered in your community.

1) Engage the HOA
HOA groups often create and enforce policies for the residential communities they manage. Most likely, you are not the only resident observing the trash being littered around your neighborhood and there is a high chance that other neighbors share the discontent. If your townhouse community has an HOA, bringing this issue to their attention at the next HOA meeting may be a good way to start. With enough support from other residents and approval from the HOA board, guidelines can be set restricting any trash to be littered. HOA often also have the power, written into the contractual agreements signed by residents before move-in, to enforce rules they set. Penalties for residents refusing to comply with rules may range from thousands of dollars in fees to eviction. If new HOA rules making improper disposal of trash can be set, then residents will have to eventually comply, assuming the root cause is from within the community. HOAs may even help lead preventative strategies attempting to proactively address the problem. Some strategies include the installation of waste baskets for general use, increasing the frequency of waste management services, installing street signs, and/or employing third-party street cleaning services. 

2) Establish a Neighborhood Watch Group
A neighborhood watch, also called a crime watch is an organized group of civilians devoted to crime and vandalism prevention within a neighborhood, including littering. Similar to HOA organizations, members of watch groups are often intrinsically motivated to maintain a clean neighborhood and share the same common goals. Neighborhood watch groups can be as informal or formal as one would like, although informal methods may be easier to start if your community does not have such a group in place already. Typically, informal watch groups involve select community residents patrolling and monitoring the community looking out for any suspicious activity, crime, or other behavior breaking rules. A schedule is usually shared between volunteers listing out availabilities, procedures in case of emergencies, and contact information, including local law enforcement. Having an active neighborhood watch group monitoring the community will likely deter the culprits. Although the initial purpose of starting a watch group may be to catch and deter litterers, it is possible that the group also inadvertently encounters more serious and dangerous criminals who have gone unnoticed in the past. Depending on the danger of the threats, and if the watch group volunteers are inexperienced or untrained in handling more threatening situations, then risks can quickly escalate beyond what was anticipated. Therefore, the safety of the volunteers within the group is an important concern and should remain a high priority. 

3) Contact local law enforcement
Law enforcement will likely be able to assist in preventing trash to be littered in your community. Law enforcement is a public service and it can be argued that trash is impeding the well-being of the local public. A big advantage of involving law enforcement over creating a local neighborhood watch group is that the former has extensive experience and training in dealing with a wide range of threats, while the latter may not. For example, if the litterers also coincidentally happen to be wanted fugitives then law enforcement would be prepared to apprehend the criminals safely away from the community residents. Another advantage of involving law enforcement to eliminate trash being littered in your community is that they can adjust their levels of engagement depending on the severity of the issues. If the trash being littered is largely immaterial or non-threatening, then they may elect to install street signs warning culprits of the consequences of littering or occasionally patrol the street in marked police cars. Law enforcement may even leave a marked police car in plain sight within the community since the sight of a police car is known to reduce the chances of criminal activity in most cases. However, if trash being littered is significantly harming the residents (e.g., hazardous materials, food waste, heavy items, etc.), then law enforcement will likely elect to increase their engagement and may even dedicate an officer present at all times. As illustrated, some of the benefits of contacting law enforcement are the flexibility of engagement, the depth of their expertise, and nearly unlimited resources in combatting the littering issue.', 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: My debit card was involved in a data breach, and I lost $3,000. The bank says I'll get it back, but they don't know how long it'll take. What are some things I can do to better protect myself in the future?
messages:

 {'content': 'I'm sorry to hear this! Suspicious charges can be frustrating. Here are some recommendations for how to best protect your funds:

1) Stick to large, reputable banks and institutions. Although there is some data that suggests large banks are more likely to be targets of cyberattacks, they are also more prepared to handle them. Small, hometown banks often have less rigorous security standards and a smaller amount of available cash flow, meaning that they cannot immediately refund your funds and must wait until the dispute has settled.

2) Complete all purchases on a credit card, rather than a debit card. Although this seems counter-intuitive, as credit cards incur interest, they are also much safer. When disputing a credit card charge, you do not have to pay the funds until the dispute is settled. It's much easier to stop a charge than it is to recover funds once they have departed your account. Furthermore, interest is only paid on credit card charges that carry over to the next month or interest period, and some might even offer perks like cash back on purchases or point accrual towards future discounts or interest rates.

3) Use a verified transaction company, such as Paypal, when completing online purchases. Paypal has buyer protection and can handle disputes efficiently. Smaller sites with their own payment processors might not be as safe and verified as they assert themselves to be, nor will they be as conveniently reachable in the event of a dispute. 

4) Refrain from linking your bank account, debit card, or credit card to any services. Saving your information in their system creates a database that can be breached at any point in the future if your password is discovered or the company suffers a cyberattack. Typing your information each time makes this less likely, although not impossible. 

5) Change your passwords frequently and don't save them on websites or in your browser. Using strong passwords and changing them frequently significantly reduces the likelihood they will be involved in a company's data breach. You may not be immediately notified of a compromised password, so don't reuse them.

6) Diversify your accounts. As the saying goes, "don't keep all of your eggs in one basket." Your checking account should be used for flowing cash, while your savings account should hold any lump sums that you may need access to in emergencies. Beyond your emergency fund, you can store cash in certificates of deposits (CDs) or investments that earn interest.

7) Stay aware of your account and purchases. Turn on purchase alerts if your bank offers them. Balance your checkbook and review your account frequently to notice any strange charges. The earlier these charges are caught, the easier they are resolved.

I hope these suggestions help better protect your funds in the future!', 'role': 'assistant'}]

Write it in a casual, upbeat and energetic voice and use personal anecdotal experience as the framework to explain these concepts. ', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': 'Hey yogis! 

Today we're going to talk about the secret to nailing arm balances and inversion poses. Before you roll your eyes and groan that you're not strong enough, skinny enough, or flexible enough, hear me out! I'm convinced that none of these challenges are actually deal breakers when it comes to unlocking these intimidating poses, and hopefully, by the end of this post, you will be, too. 

Every time I unlock a new, difficult pose--whether it's a crow pose, handstand, or flying splits--I'm always shocked at how easy it feels. That's because these poses don't actually require as much strength or flexibility as we usually believe they do. Sure, core strength is an integral element of any balance pose, but you don't need washboard abs. Getting into these poses in the first place doesn't require extraordinary strength, but it does require the following: 

-Alignment. Standing on your hands is relatively easy when you stack your shoulders over your wrists and hips over your shoulders. You'll run into trouble if your hands are too close together or too far apart. 
-Engaged core. Even if your abs are fairly weak, you can still activate the core as you land in the pose to build strength while practicing and to make your body feel lighter (just like in "light as a feather, stiff as a board").
-Hand posture. To balance on the hands, your palms need to be slightly tented and fingers spread, gripping the mat like claws. This gives your fingers room to move and steady your balance if you feel like you might fall, whereas if they're already flat on the mat, they can't do anything to help you. 
-Drishti. Holding a focal point with your gaze is one of the most important keys to balance poses. If your eyes start wandering around the room, you will start wobbling. It also is helpful to send your gaze forward in balances and inversions. If you look down, you will likely fall down. 
-Belief. Fear is probably the single greatest hurdle that aspiring arm balancers need to overcome. It's understandable--no one wants to fall on their face. But you might be surprised how effective it is to relax, visualize yourself in a pose, and even use little cheats to prove to yourself that you're capable. ', 'role': 'assistant'}]

 {'content': 'In the world of mental health and wellness, phobias are considered a kind of anxiety disorder that can cause someone to have an extreme fear of places, objects, animals, people, situations, and things. The fears are often irrational and difficult to explain, but exposure to the subject of a phobia can cause severe reactions, like the urge to run away or lash out violently. 

Some phobias are more widely accepted and well-known than others. Arachnophobia, for instance, is the extreme fear of spiders, and it affects up to 15 percent of the world’s population. Other common phobias include ophidiophobia (the fear of snakes), acrophobia (the fear of heights), and cynophobia (the fear of dogs). 

Some phobias, while uncommon, are still real and scary to the people that suffer from them. Five lesser-known phobias include: 

•	Alektorophobia (the fear of chickens). 
•	Globophobia (the fear of balloons). 
•	Podophobia (the fear of feet). 
•	Pedophobia (the fear of small children)
•	Phobophobia (the fear of fear) 

While some phobias may seem strange or silly to other people, they are often a source of extreme anxiety and insecurity for sufferers. The cause of each phobia can vary depending on the person. While some may have had negative experiences that caused extreme fear, others could associate their general anxiety disorder with a specific phobia because their brain latches onto that fear at the moment. 

Through psychotherapy and consistent behavioral therapy, most phobias can be either completely cured or lessened. The sufferer has to be dedicated to finding treatment and healing from their fears. There’s no linear method of treatment since every phobia sufferer is different and has different reasons for the fear that they feel. 

In most cases, exposure therapy is a method of overcoming any phobia. This means that a sufferer has to get comfortable with the object of their fear before they can heal and overcome their phobia. In other cases, anxiety medications can help lessen the extreme fear and visceral reactions associated with certain phobias.

Then came the loud FLOP! of the unfurling parachute, and everything sped up again for a brief second. The harness yanked against my body with a jolt that made my teeth chatter. Once my acceleration had stabilized, though, it was back to slow motion.

prompt: I've been balancing a day job and freelance writing for a while, and I want to know how to make the transition to freelancing full-time. How do I do so? Can you make me a list that goes through some helpful steps in this process?

 {'content': "Good luck with your transition into freelancing! Here's some things you can do to give yourself the best chance of success

1. Figure out finances - Find out how much you typically spend each month including bills and figure out how much money you need to bring in every month to make ends meet. 
2. Get a regular client - You should find a client with regular work while you're still working your day job. This client acts as a sort of retainer because you know that you can be assured to have regular work while you're with them. 5. Make an elevator pitch - Ask yourself exactly what you want to bring to the table, and make this clear on your website site. Ingredients List:
* 1-2 packs of chicken breast tenders
* 1/2c buttermilk
* 1/5c pickle juice
* 2c all-purpose flour
* 2tbs each of salt, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and white pepper
* 1/2c honey
* 1/4c buffalo or Tabasco sauce
* 2tsp butter
* Oil of your choice for frying

1. Marinate your chicken: Place your chicken, buttermilk, pickle juice, and half of all spices in a bag or container and allow it to sit for at least 1 hour.

6. Once your last batch of tenders is frying, start preparing your sauce by combining the honey, buffalo sauce, and butter in a small saucepan.
7. Cook over medium heat until it starts to bubble and thicken. Once the desired consistency is achieved remove from the heat.

messages:
[{'content': "Write a recipe for a pink donut like the one on The Simpsons. Make it vegan! List the ingredients first and then the instructions. I'm also allergic to oats so don't use oat milk.", 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': "Donuts:

- 2 cups all-purpose flour
- 1/2 cup granulated sugar
- 2 teaspoons baking powder
- 1/2 teaspoon baking soda
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 3/4 cup unsweetened almond milk
- 1/4 cup melted coconut oil
- 2 teaspoons apple cider vinegar
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

Pink glaze:

- 2 cups powdered sugar
- 1/4 cup unsweetened almond milk
- 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
- Pink food coloring 

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a donut pan with coconut oil or non-stick spray.
2. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt until well combined.
3. In a separate bowl, combine the almond milk, melted coconut oil, apple cider vinegar, and vanilla extract. Stir well.
4. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until just combined. Avoid overmixing.
5. Add a few drops of pink food coloring to the batter and stir until the color is evenly distributed. Keep adding food-colored for your desired shade of pink!
6. Spoon the batter into a piping bag or a ziplock bag with a corner snipped off. Pipe the batter into the prepared donut pan, filling each cavity about two-thirds full.
7. Place the donut pan in the preheated oven and bake for 12-15 minutes. If you can insert a toothpick and it comes out clean, you're good!
8. While the donuts are baking, prepare the pink glaze. In a medium-sized bowl, whisk together the powdered sugar, almond milk, and vanilla extract until smooth and well combined. Add a few drops of pink food coloring and mix until the glaze is pink. Add more for a deeper shade of pink!
9. Once the donuts have cooled slightly, remove them from the pan and dip each one into the pink glaze, making sure to coat both sides. Place the glazed donuts on a wire rack set over a baking sheet to allow any excess glaze to drip off.
10. If desired, you can sprinkle some vegan-friendly sprinkles or edible glitter on top of the glaze for extra decoration.
11. Let the glaze set for about 10-15 minutes before serving. ", 'role': 'assistant'}]

 {'content': "Mua ha ha ha ha! They may think I'm mad, but I will give you the greatest coconut bundt cake recipe ever created!

First, make sure that you have a bundt pan. This recipe is perfectly calculated for a 6-cup pan to make two cakes, but you can use one 12-cup pan to make one larger cake as long as you increase the overall cook time to an hour.

Here are the ingenious ingredients that will make a cake so good the world will think you're an evil genius like me:

1. Cake Ingredients
    a. 2 teaspoons of coconut extract. This is the most important one!
    b. 1 teaspoon of baking powder
    c. 4 eggs
    d. 2 1/4 cups of flour
    e. 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract
    f. 1/2 a cup of milk
    g. 1 cup of sweetened shredded coconut
    h. 2 1/2 cups of sugar
    i. 1/2 a teaspoon of salt
    j. 1 cup of butter (softened)
2. Glaze ingredients
   a. 1 1/2 cups of powdered sugar
   b. 1 teaspoon of coconut extract
   c. 2 tablespoons of milk
   d. 2 tablespoons of melted butter
3. Topping ingredients
   a. 2/3 a cup of shredded sweetened coconut

Now that you have gathered the ingredients for your cooking experiment, it is time to begin bringing your creation to life! Mua ha ha ha ha!

- Preheat your oven to 325 degrees F. Grease and lightly flour your bundt pans and set up your oven rack in the middle of the oven. Setting up all of this in advance separates normal scientists from true mad scientists!
- Whisk your flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium mixing bowl and set it aside.
- In a bigger mixing bowl, beat the butter and sugar together until they are fluffy and light. Add the eggs and two types of extract and continue to beat this new mixture until it is smooth. Add the milk and beat again on low speed. Then add the flour mix from the other bowl and beat it until the two have become one. Stir in your coconut.
- Pour this batter into your bundt pans and put them in the oven for fifty to fifty-five minutes. You should have plenty of time to plot your next experiment while you're waiting!
- When your cake is finished, set the pan on a wire rack to cool for fifteen minutes. After this, place the cooling rack over the top of the pan and flip the whole thing over. The cake should drop out with no problem if you have followed my brilliant instructions correctly!
- Now, the time of the glaze has arrived. Melt the butter in a glass bowl, then add the rest of the three ingredients and whisk it all together until it is smooth. Add more milk to thin it or more powdered sugar to thicken it.

 {'content': 'In Chicago, tavern-style pizza originated as a way for the city's workers to have a little bite with their post-shift beer. Let's dig into what makes Chicago's tavern-style pie so delicious: 

- Crust: The crust of a tavern-style pizza is inarguably its defining characteristic. Thin and crispy, it has a slightly thicker and sturdier base than a traditional thin-crust pizza. This comes from the dough being pre-stretched and rolled out before being topped and baked. The end product is often referred to as a "cracker-like" crust due to its crispy texture. It's not uncommon to see a crust that crumbs and flakes like a saltine!

- Shape and Size: Tavern-style pizza is typically baked in a round shape, cut into small square pieces. These are commonly known as "party-cut" or "tavern-cut" slices.

- Cheese: Unlike traditional thin-crust pizza, tavern-style pizza usually features a layer of cheese extending to the edge of the crust. The cheese is typically a combination of low-moisture mozzarella and cheddar, which melts and caramelizes, creating a slightly crispy and flavorful cheese edge. Combine that with the crispiness of the thin crust underneath, and it's easy to understand why some folks sprint to the corner pieces.

- Toppings: Tavern-style pizza often features traditional toppings such as Italian sausage, green peppers, onions, and mushrooms. However, the toppings are usually applied generously and heartily, creating a more substantial pizza compared to some other thin crust styles. It can make those center square pieces feel much heavier as well!

 {'content': "Here are four tips on how to ask for a raise at work for someone who's never done that before along with an explanation of what each tip is meant to accomplish. Each tip aims to keep your raise request professional and polite, but also firm and direct:

1. Find any and all positive feedback since your last performance review. Once you've made your meeting request, prepare for it by finding any and all evidence that your recent performance has surpassed expectations. In order to be both firm and direct in your meeting, you will need to be able to present concrete examples of how you've performed at an above-average level. Keep in mind, your boss may not interpret your evidence in exactly the same way as you do, so ensure that you remain calm and stick to the facts no matter what they say.
 
2. Come prepared with data and numbers. In order to present the most persuasive and compelling case for your raise, it's best to be able to clearly point to specific numbers and data that demonstrate your value to the organization. By presenting specific metrics and tangible goals you've accomplished, you will be able to show visually that you have outperformed your current salary. Relying on data also helps keep your meeting objective, removing personal bias or emotion from the equation and allowing you and your boss to focus on the numbers. 

3. Explain what you’ll bring to the team in the coming year. Once you've discussed your past performance, be sure to also focus on your goals for the future. Frame your raise request as an investment, something that will pay off for the organization by demonstrating a clear commitment to one of its top performers. Remember to remain calm and clear as you talk about the future in order to avoid over-selling your commitment and having it come off as insincere.

4. Identify the salary range you’ll ask for and know how to justify it. One of the most awkward parts of a meeting to discuss a raise is inevitably the question of how much exactly to ask for. This is definitely something you will want to think about beforehand and be prepared to justify based on the evidence you will present. It's important that when it comes time to discuss the specific parameters of your raise request, you be able to point to specific, objective reasons why your numbers are fair so that your boss can best understand and hopefully agree with your point of view.

prompt: Im 16 and looking for my first job, can you brainstorm 10 places to apply that arent retail or fast food, i don't want to do those, thanks u

1. Offices. Many offices will hire high school students because they perform easy, routine work, such as typing, entering data, and answering the phone.
2. Restaurants. Family-owned restaurants, diners, and coffee shops often hire high school students to help them make some extra money during the semester or over the summer.
3. Libraries. Library jobs are easy to learn. See if you can find a job working at the front desk.
4. Used bookstores. Most used bookstores have local owners who could hire you temporarily, possibly offering a permanent position after you graduate.
5. Delis. Visit the local butcher, deli, or meat market to possibly get some food service experience on your resume.
6. Post offices. These and other government jobs provide decent wages, so call your local post office to see if they're hiring.
7. Banks. Your local bank might offer a few shifts after work or over the weekend.
8. Hobby stores. Locally owned stores for hobbyists, such as quilters and thrift shoppers, don't advertise for new employees often, but you can get in touch and see if they need some help.
9. Medical clinics. Go online to look for open secretarial and office assistant positions.
10. Churches. Many churches rely on volunteer work, but you could still call around and see if anyone needs an employee. If you currently go to church, you already have a place to ask.

Additionally, see if your high school has a student work program. You might earn a paid position as a tutor, library assistant, or office worker. Your school might also host job fairs where you can meet potential employers in your area. prompt: I've been thinking about taking martial arts for self-defense and exercise. What are 5 martial art disciplines that can offer me these things?
messages:
[{'content': "I've been thinking about taking martial arts for self-defense and exercise. What are 5 martial art disciplines that can offer me these things?", 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': 'While all martial arts are designed to give you a good workout and promote self-defense, here is a list of 5 martial arts that you could learn that will give you the most "bang for your buck":

1. Brazilian Jiujitsu - One of the best martial arts for both self-defense and a killer workout, Brazilian Jiujitsu (BJJ) provides practitioners with real-world self-defense. Many fights end up on the ground, and those who are not used to maneuvering on their backs will find themselves defenseless, trying to protect against attacks from above. In addition to the self-defense skills you'll learn in BJJ, you'll also get a tremendous workout that is sure to tax your aerobic and anaerobic systems. 
2. Muay Thai - This martial art from Thailand is such a huge sport that modern mixed martial artists have incorporated it into their training regimens. Muay Thai is a form of kickboxing that also makes use of elbow and knee strikes, as well as throws and leg sweeps. A good defensive martial art teaches you to strike with multiple different parts of your body, and Muay Thai does just that. You'll also get a great cardio workout doing several rounds of Muay Thai kickboxing against a sparring partner or potential opponent.
3. Kung Fu/Wushu - Kung Fu and Wushu are Chinese martial arts that have been around for centuries. While Kung Fu can mean anything that requires skill (i.e., you can have good "Kung Fu" washing dishes or driving a car), the martial art of Kung Fu is specifically a fighting art that teaches multiple stances, punches, and kicks, the most popular of which mimic the movements of animals like the snake, the crane, and the tiger. A great workout can be had practicing stances and forms that require you to stand in unusual positions, such as a horse stance, for several minutes at a time. Wushu (the competitive version of Kung Fu) stresses the importance of performative martial art through high jumps and kicks, twirls, flips, and other choreographed moves.
4. Judo - Much like the other grappling arts, Judo is a Japanese art that involves throwing one's opponent and also using their momentum and body weight against themselves. In addition to throws, Judo also practices grappling (both on the ground and while standing) and submissions (joint locks, strangles). Judo can be likened to lifting weights due to having to throw and carry your opponent, which can be tiring.
5. Karate - Karate, like its Chinese counterpart in Kung Fu, is a martial art that involves the use of strikes and stances. However, Karate's development in Japan created a martial art that promotes striking opponents hard and fast; straight punches and kicks that snap from the waist are favored over the flowery techniques of Kung Fu and Wushu. As with all the other martial arts listed above, Karate offers a great workout practicing striking and forms.', 'role': 'assistant'}]

5. Flower Urchin

Peter

Hypothesis

A pair of loops, hereafter referred to as "bunny ears", when crossed at a common point and pulled taught, might affix a shoe to its appropriate foot for a period of up to twelve hours, or until manually released.

Materials and Methods

One pair of tennis shoes - Velcro (Control)
Twelve-Inch nylon braided shoe lace - Brown

Results

By going to bed and getting up at the same time every day (including weekends), you can make your body's sleep-wake cycle more consistent.
2. Monitor your diet -- Going to bed either hungry or overly full can impair sleep quality, so you should try to avoid any heavy meals just before bed. You should also exercise caution with nicotine, caffeine, and alcohol consumption. Nicotine and caffeine take hours to wear off, and alcohol can disrupt sleep later in the night.
3. Establish a restful environment -- Rooms that are cool, dark, and quiet are more conducive to restful sleep while light-emitting screens tend to be disruptive. 5. Get regular physical activity -- While you shouldn't be too active close to bedtime when you're trying to wind down, being physically active as part of your daily routine can promote better rest. Spending time outside is a great way to do this and provides other health benefits as well.
6. Reduce stress -- Lingering concerns won't do your sleep schedule any favors. One way to deal with these is to journal what's on your mind before bed so you can set it aside for the next day.  {'content': "Common Literary Devices You Must Know as a Writer

As a writer, it’s not enough to just write a bunch of words to tell a story. You have to know how to use literary devices to make your writing pop. Here are some commonly used literary devices that every writer must know.

Anthropomorphism
I love animals. And what's not to love? They're cute, cuddly, and downright hilarious at times. But what if I told you that you could turn an animal into a character? Well, with anthropomorphism, you can!
Anthropomorphism is the act of giving an animal human-like qualities, such as emotions, speech, and cognition.
Take Disney's The Lion King, for example. All of the characters are animals, but they talk, have feelings, and experience personal growth.

Anastrophe
Anastrophe is a fancy way of rearranging words for emphasis. You change the order of words to emphasize a specific point or idea. Yoda from Star Wars is a perfect example of anastrophe. Instead of saying, ‘You must unlearn what you have learned’, he says, Learn, you must, what you have unlearned. It adds a level of importance to the statement.

Anaphora
Do you ever find yourself repeating the same word or phrase? If yes, you're using anaphora! Anaphora is when you repeat a word or phrase at the beginning of consecutive sentences. It's often used in speeches and poetry to emphasize a point and make it more memorable.
One of the most famous examples of anaphora comes from Martin Luther King Jr.'s I Have a Dream speech, where he repeats the phrase ‘I have a dream’ eight times.

Alliteration
You must have heard of alliteration – it’s the literary device that uses repetitive sounds at the beginning of words in a sentence or phrase. It's a technique that can add musicality and rhythm to your writing. Alliteration can create a sense of unity, emphasis, and resonance.
Don’t overdo it, though – use it sparingly and purposefully. Too much alliteration can make your writing seem forced or gimmicky.

Allegory
An allegory is a story that has a hidden meaning that's used to communicate a moral or political message. It can convey complex ideas simply and entertainingly.", 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: Can you tell me about the An-71? Why does it look backwards? What was it for?
messages:
[{'content': 'Can you tell me about the An-71? Why does it look backwards? What was it for?', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': 'It was a prototype aircraft intended to fill the airborne warning and control system (AWACS) role for the Soviet Union to serve the needs of their fighter-bombers and attack aircraft. Three prototypes were built, but the planes never entered active service. 

The An-71 was based on the Antonov An-72 cargo plane. That type had high-mounted jet engines because it was built for short takeoffs and landings on imperfect runways in austere locations. Placing the engines up high made them less likely to suck debris off the ground and damage the turbine blades.

When it came time to modify that design to carry a large 360-degree radar system, designers decided to try integrating it into the tail fin rather than placing the round radome on an extra set of mounting brackets. Any feature that you place in the way of airflow creates drag, so eliminating the need for extra uprights would improve the plane’s handling and range. 

Engineers couldn’t just put the radome on the standard tail, though. The radar equipment is heavy and alters the plane’s aerodynamics. Sweeping the tail forward placed the radome closer to the plane’s center of gravity and thus improved its stability. It was considered a major redesign of the tail section (the horizontal stabilizers also had to be repositioned).

Antonov briefly considered creating a naval version of the An-71 as well, but it quickly became apparent that adapting it for carrier operations would demand too many redesigned features. That project was scrapped.

The An-71 never entered service in part because of problems developing the radar itself. Its death knell, though, was the collapse of the Soviet Union. Funding for the project evaporated, so it was abruptly halted. At the turn of the 21st century, Antonov in now-independent Ukraine tried to resurrect the project in order to sell An-71s to India, but that also fell through.', 'role': 'assistant'}]

 {'content': '- Down syndrome is a condition in which a person has an extra chromosome.

- Typically babies are born with 46 chromosomes, but babies with Down syndrome are born with an extra chromosome 21.

- The extra chromosome affects how the baby's body and brain will develop and can cause mental and physical challenges.

- Another name for Down syndrome is "Trisomy 21". "Trisomy" refers to the extra chromosome, and 21 is the actual chromosome that has two copies.

- Down Syndrome affects about 1 in 700 babies in the United States.

- There are three types of Down syndrome: Trisomy 21 (95% of cases, described above), Translocation Down syndrome (the extra chromosome is attached to another chromosome), and Mosaic Down syndrome (some cells have three copies instead of 2). 

- Symptoms of Down syndrome include mild to moderately low IQ, slow speech, flattened face, almond-shaped eyes that slant up, short neck, small ears, white spots on the iris of the eye, small hands and feet, poor muscle tone or loose joints, short height, and a tongue that tends to stick out.', 'role': 'assistant'}]

 {'content': "A civilization known as Gobekli Tepe, which is located in modern-day Turkey, was built 6,000 years before Stonehenge. It is heralded as one of the first sites of man-made monumental architecture in the world. On top of a limestone plateau, a German archaeologist named Klaus Schmidt was the first to discover over 20 circular stone enclosures. The largest was almost 65 feet across, with two elaborately carved 18-foot pillars in the middle. The pillars have distinctive T-shapes and are reminiscent of the human form. Some of the pillars contain reliefs that depict items of clothing and wild animals. The nature of stone tools and other artifacts found at the site show that the monoliths were built by hunter-gatherers. At that time in history, creating these immense pillars would involve using wood and stone tools to shape the limestone, then creating some sort of pulley system using rope, log beams, and a lot of manpower.

Originally, the apparent lack of residences led Schmidt to believe that the site was used solely for religious rituals, a place where nomadic bands would join together for periodic building projects and great feasts. This was a significant claim, given the time when the site was built. Remember, this was a transitional period in human history. Hunter-gathers, who had been living off the land for generations, were developing into societies that were beginning to grow their food intentionally and domesticate the animals around them. it had long been believed that rituals and religion were luxuries that developed only well after humans settled into these new societies. This discovery, however, showed that perhaps complex religion and social organization actually came before settlement and agriculture. Perhaps it was the very needs imposed by the religious rituals themselves - coming together to build the statues required large gatherings where people needed to be fed, thus the need to make food supplies more predictable by domesticating plants and animals -  that prompted the shift towards the Neolithic Revolution. 

However, in 2017, new discoveries changed the message of Gobekli Tepe. Work began to erect fabric-and-steel shelters to cover the central monumental buildings to make the site more comfortable for visiting tourists. As teams dug deeper into the bedrock than ever before, they made a shocking discovery. The digs revealed evidence of houses and year-round settlement, suggesting that instead of an isolated temple visited only on special occasions, Gobekli Tepe was a lively village with large, special buildings at the center. A rainwater collection system was also discovered, along with tools for grinding grain and even brewing beer. Since then, archaeologists working in the surrounding countryside have found at least a dozen other hilltop sites with similar pairs of T-shaped pillars, dating from around the same period. 

So what do these discoveries mean? Well, instead of the building project launching the transition to farming, perhaps Gobleki Tepe was an attempt by hunter-gatherers to cling to their way of life amidst a world that was changing around them. Evidence shows that settlements on other hills in the region were experimenting with domestication plants and animals, while the people of Gobleki Tepe appear to have been resisting the change. A sentimental reminder of a way of life that was quickly disappearing, Gobleki Tepe reminds us that humanity today is not really that different from humanity 11,000 years ago.
