messages:
[{'content': 'Make up an easy-to-follow recipe for a classic and mouthwatering cheesecake.', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': 'Classic Cheesecake Recipe

Ingredients

- 2 cups graham cracker crumbs
- 1/3 cup white sugar
- 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted
- 4 (8 oz.) packages of cream cheese, softened
- 1 1/4 cups white sugar
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 4 large eggs
- 1/3 cup heavy cream

Instructions

1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease the bottom and sides of a 9-inch springform pan.

2. In a medium bowl, mix the graham cracker crumbs, 1/3 cup of sugar, and melted butter until well combined. Press the mixture into the bottom of the prepared pan.

3. In a large bowl, beat the cream cheese until smooth and creamy. Gradually add in the 1 1/4 cups of sugar, beating until well combined. Mix in the vanilla extract.

4. Beat in the eggs, one at a time, making sure each egg is fully incorporated before adding the next.

5. Mix in the heavy cream until the mixture is smooth and creamy.

6. Pour the cheesecake batter into the prepared crust. Tap the pan gently on the counter to release any air bubbles.

7. Bake the cheesecake for 45-50 minutes, or until the center is almost set but still jiggles slightly when shaken.

8. Remove the cheesecake from the oven and let it cool to room temperature. Once cooled, cover the cheesecake with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.

9. When ready to serve, remove the cheesecake from the refrigerator and run a knife around the edge of the pan to loosen the cheesecake. Remove the sides of the springform pan.

messages:
[{'content': "Write the introduction to a post for my parenting blog about positive behavior that parents should strive to exhibit. It should feel personal and like I am commiserating with and relating to the parents reading my blog. I have two kids and I often talk about them and what I've learned as a parent. I want it to feel warm and encouraging and positive and light but not unrealistic. I just need the beginning of the article to get me started. Write the introduction and the first couple of points, then I'll take over. I want these to be the first two points:
1. Be consistent.
2. Be available. ", 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': 'It's overwhelming sometimes. 

"Don't be too strict." "Don't be too relaxed." "Don't do this." "Don't do that." 

I don't know about you, but I look at those words and think: That's enough of that. We hear enough about what we're NOT supposed to be as parents. Today, let's talk about some behavior we SHOULD model for our children. 

Here are some parenting wins that I strive for every day:

1. Being consistent.
How would you feel if the speed limit on the freeway changed every time you drove on it? But there were no signs - so you wouldn't know the limit had changed until you saw the flashing blue and red lights in the rearview mirror. Oof. I would be mad. I would be frustrated. I might even throw a temper tantrum when the cop tried to hand me a ticket. 
Our kids value consistency as much as we do — they just don't know how to ask for it. Setting clear limits and consequences helps your kids feel loved and safe. They can have confidence in their actions when they're behaving well, and they'll likely react with less anger when they're disciplined because they can understand why —  even if they don't agree with you. 

2. Being available.
There is absolutely no substitute for quality time. You might have noticed that a quick "Is there anything you want to talk about?" asked in a rush before school drop-off probably doesn't result in a whole lot of open discussions. Asking "How was school?" on the ride home might not get much of a response either. But taking an after-dinner stroll with no expectations? Eating breakfast together on the weekends with no distractions? Will open the door to relaxed, enjoyable conversations with your kids. And if they approach you wanting to talk, do your best to make time RIGHT THEN if it's at all possible. Show them they're important to you. And if you don't have time right at that moment, make a plan for when you'll talk more and then stick to it. Being available to your kids when they're young — even though the problems of a three-year-old may not seem life-changing — will start a healthy pattern of communication that will continue into their teen years.', 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: I recently became the property manager of a smaller apartment complex. We have a lot of communal grassy areas that are not currently being used. What are some ways I can improve these areas? I would like to make the complex more desirable to prospective renters and improve the quality of life for our existing tenants. I need a bullet-point list of 4 ideas, please.
messages:
[{'content': 'I recently became the property manager of a smaller apartment complex. We have a lot of communal grassy areas that are not currently being used. What are some ways I can improve these areas? I would like to make the complex more desirable to prospective renters and improve the quality of life for our existing tenants. I need a bullet-point list of 4 ideas, please.', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': "No problem! Here are some ideas on how to use the land at your apartment complex:

* A dog park: If your apartment is pet friendly, a dog park is a great way to utilize the free space you have. Dogs who live in apartments don't get to enjoy the freedom or have the space to run around as dogs with fenced-in yards do, and they are often required to be leashed when they are on the apartment grounds with their owners. A fenced dog park allows dogs to have more freedom, run around safely, and play and socialize with other dogs. The pet parents at your complex will thank you!

* A picnic area: Having a communal picnic area at your apartment is a great idea. You can install a communal grill and picnic benches, giving your residents a place to gather and enjoy time outside instead of being cooped up inside. This also helps foster a sense of community where neighbors can get to know and befriend one another. If your tenants have their friends or family over for a gathering at the picnic area, this is a great way to show off your amenities to the wider community, which can in turn lead to more interest in your apartments. 

* A playground: A play area is a great way to attract renters with young children and will be a popular addition for children already residing in your apartments. There are many kinds of play equipment you can install, including swings, slides, and climbing equipment. Make sure that the playground has a soft surface such as sand or solid rubber to ensure safety. 

* A garden: One of your vacant grassy areas could be transformed into a beautiful garden. Whilst living in apartments, it's hard to find peace or privacy and sometimes you might just need somewhere relaxing to be alone with your thoughts. To achieve this, you could create a tranquil garden area for the residents to sit in and admire. Plant some trees and flower beds, install a fountain or water feature, and add some wind chimes and benches. This will help your apartment look more attractive and cared for to potential future residents.", 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: Write a review of a fun trip to Antarctica.
messages:
[{'content': 'Write a review of a fun trip to Antarctica.', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': "My trip to Antarctica was a once-in-a-lifetime experience! The natural beauty of Antarctica is breathtaking. We left the southern tip of South America on a cozy expedition vessel and were at sea for several days. There was onboard entertainment that made at-sea days go by quickly - lectures, documentaries, a well-stocked library, citizen science programs, and plenty of marine life and birds. We had several social events in the evenings, like a trivia competition, a dessert tasting, and a dance party. It took several days to cross the notoriously rough waters of the Drake Passage. I won't lie, I struggled. I had to see the ship's doctor for medication. Once we arrived around the Antarctica peninsula, we were more sheltered and it was smoother. We spent several days exploring various locations along the peninsula, including my dream visit to a scientific research station, several historic sites, and many wildlife hotspots before our return.

The biggest highlight of my trip to Antarctica was seeing such a wide variety of wildlife up close and personal. When I say up close and personal, I mean that they walk right up to you. We saw so many colonies of penguins, seals, whales, and of seabirds. Visiting the penguin colonies was different than expected, as it really stunk. Those little cuties projectile poop everywhere. The smell gets in your clothes and hair. Bring Febreeze! The moment that stands out the most from the trip was this trip to the peninsula in a zodiac where a humpback whale swam right next to us most of the way. I could see his barnacles in detail, he was so close! It was life-changing. 

The scenery in Antarctica was simply wild, massive glaciers, snow-blanketed mountains, and icebergs that are measured in kilometers instead of meters. It was mind-blowing daily. 

I cannot talk about this trip without sharing the unique soundtrack we heard.

Some of my favorites were:
* The glaciers rumble and crack like thunder as they calve ice into the sea.
* The exhale of air from a whale’s blowhole.
* The slapping of little penguin feet as they follow each other down their established roadways. (This is probably my favorite soundtrack of the trip.)

Overall, my trip to Antarctica was an unforgettable experience that I will revisit in my mind for the rest of my life. ", 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: I'd like you to write a first-person point of view sports article, like the kind you post online or send to the local news, about why Sammy Sosa should be in the hall of fame.
messages:

 {'content': "Sammy Sosa deserves to be in the Baseball Hall of Fame and it is a travesty that he is let out. Yeah, I'm a north sider from Chicago and I bleed Cubby blue but Sosa is nothing short of a legend. He brought baseball back from the brink of obscurity and now baseball just wants to use him as a scapegoat.

Every baseball fan from the 90s remembers Sammy Sosa and Mark McGwire chasing Roger Maris' record and finally eclipsing it. The year was 1998 and it captivated the whole nation. Two men from historic rival teams going all summer long trying to outlast and outhit the other. It was nothing short of epic and without Sosa's race, baseball would not be the popular sport that it is today.

His resume is impressive too. He hit over 600 home runs which not even 10 players in the entire history of the sport have done. He also won an MVP award in 1998 and numerous other awards like Silver Sluggers and was a perennial all-star. Sammy Sosa embodied baseball in the late 90s and early 00s. But now the industry is doing him wrong by trying to sweep him and all those other great hitters under the rug.

Yes, I know it was the steroid era.  But everyone was juicing and we all knew it. It was that unspoken compact that nobody ever brought up because it didn't need to be said. The league knew it and wanted to profit from all the eyes on the sport, we fans knew it but we were enjoying the competition too much to care, and the players knew it but were reaching new heights in their careers. I'm not saying it was okay but I am saying the players we loved shouldn't be the ones bearing the blame for it all. I, as a fan, share in the culpability and still want the best of that era in the hall. Players like Sosa.

So please don't let his legacy fade away. The numbers back it up and if you want to shave off 100 home runs he's still an amazing athlete. Plus you add on how much he helped revive America's past-time and it can't be denied that Sosa belongs in the hallowed halls of Cooperstown. ", 'role': 'assistant'}]

Epilepsy can be caused by stroke, infection, tumors, or unknown origin. Many people use medications, diet, or lifestyle changes to control seizure activity. Seizures can happen on their own or be triggered by something specific to the individual. In 2015, three million adults and 470,000 children had epilepsy. 

Many people are unaware that there are three types of seizures: generalized onset, focal onset, and unknown onset. Generalized onset seizures affect both sides of the brain, and include tonic-clonic, Tonic means the muscles stiffen, and clonic is when muscles jerk. During a focal seizure, people are awake and at least partially aware of what is happening. This kind affects only one side of the brain.  {'content': 'Here are some of the most important factors to consider when choosing a college to attend. 

1. Your Perspective - The most important factor to consider when choosing which college you will attend is how the school makes you feel while you're there. It doesn't really matter about their programs, opportunities, and scholarships if you don't feel like you belong. The right college for you will provide an environment that is challenging to you but will also help you realize that your dreams are within your reach. 

2. Internship Opportunities
Having some hands-on experience in the field you are interested in will not only help you learn more about your future career, but it is also a great way to help you discover your passions and expand your network. Check out what internships, hands-on opportunities, research, and opportunities to study abroad the colleges on your list have to offer, and be happy with those that you are most interested in. 

3. Safety 
Not only is safety a priority on campus, but it should also be a major factor when considering the safety of your surrounding area. What types of safety measures does the school put into place? What are the surrounding towns and neighborhoods like? Knowing more about the school's safety procedures and policies when it comes to student safety can be useful when it comes to deciding if the school in question is your best fit. 

4. Academic Support and Career Services Offered 
How a college assists its students with academics is a very important factor in terms of what kind of education you will be getting. There are some schools that offer very little support and only want to provide an environment of independence, while other schools will offer things like free tutoring or writing assistance. Additionally, knowing what the school's placement rates are for jobs and postgrad schools are critical things to consider, because it offers an indication of the overall success and depth of their programs. 

5. Campus Life

Ask important questions such as "How many students live on campus?" or "What is there to do on the weekends?" These are all questions that will give you a better understanding of college life for students who attend school there. 

6. Athletics and Extracurricular Activities 
If you are interested in extracurriculars such as theatre, music, or student government, or if you love to play sports, college is an excellent time to explore brand-new passions and re-develop old hobbies. The right school for you will have the opportunity for you to do both. 

7. Majors and Minors 
Every school has a different curriculum so you should consider what you want to get out of it while you are there. You will also want to determine which majors, minors, and concentrations are offered at each school you're considering.

prompt: I need a list of editing tips for self-editing my novel. What should I be looking for?
messages:
[{'content': 'I need a list of editing tips for self-editing my novel. What should I be looking for?', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': 'Self-editing is a lot of work, but I think you can do it! Here is a list of self-editing tips: 

1. Read without editing: It might sound contradictory, but it's a good idea to read your entire manuscript before starting to edit. Keep your eyes on pacing, consistency, and character issues, but don't make any changes just yet. 

2. Look at the big picture: Before getting into the punctuation or spelling issues, look for bigger concerns such as plot holes and inconsistencies. You might also look for scenes that need to be fleshed out or character arcs that need attention. 

3. Edit for weak spots: Every writer has strengths and weaknesses, and editing with those weaknesses in mind can improve your manuscript. For example, your weakness might be detail, pacing, or dialogue. Whatever it is, pay close attention to those areas as you edit. You can also ask for feedback from a writing group, test reader, or writing partner. 

4. Look for info dumps: Look for large chunks of writing in your story and ask if the details are truly needed. If so, is there another way you can convey this information? 

5. Edit for sensory details: Remember to show, not tell when writing descriptions. Check for details relating to each of the five senses, and use strong verbs rather than adverbs. 

6: Clean up dialogue: Red your dialogue carefully to see if it feels natural and sounds like something someone would actually say. Also, check for overuse of dialogue tags like "she said," or "they yelled." Consider replacing some dialogue tags with action beats.

7: Remove repetition: Pay attention to how your sentences start, and make revisions so that they don't all start the same way. 

8: Proofread: Once you've performed the other editing steps, you can check for spelling, punctuation, and grammar mistakes. ', 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: Help me beat writer’s block! Give me a few tips on how to overcome the mental wall that keeps me from writing something awesome.
messages:
[{'content': 'Help me beat writer’s block! Give me a few tips on how to overcome the mental wall that keeps me from writing something awesome.', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': 'Writer’s block can affect anyone, from hopeful college essayists to elementary book reporters and award-winning novelists. Many creative minds chalk it up to burnout but knowing the cause doesn’t always provide the solution to get you in a clear mindset to write again. 

Read on for a few tips on how to overcome writer’s block and get back to a place of creative prowess. 

•	Seek inspiration from another writer. 

Read for fun and inspiration! Delve into a book to read the words of one of your favorite authors. Sometimes their creativity can rub off on you! 

•	Write about your feelings, your day, your family… anything to get your creativity headed in the right direction. 

Renowned poet Charles Bukowski once said, “writing about writer’s block is better than not writing at all.” As long as you are actively writing whatever comes to mind, you are making strides toward inspiration to write something brilliant. 

•	Take a step back and take care of yourself. 

Sometimes writers push themselves too hard, too far, to come up with something well-written before a deadline, either self-imposed or professional. Step back and take care of yourself in other ways to clear your mind and feel refreshed. Take a bubble bath, spend time with friends and loved ones, binge a television show… do things that make you happy without the written word. Then come back to it rejuvenated. 

•	Find a creative writing prompt that restores the thrill and fun of writing! 

“Pretend that you are an alien from another planet and you’ve just seen a cow for the first time. What are your thoughts?” 

Writing prompts can be silly, fun, and great ways to jumpstart your creativity. You don’t have to take yourself too seriously. Simply let your imagination play out on the paper. 

•	Work your brain without words. 

Burnout is a real struggle for writers, and sometimes your brain needs a break from words. This would be a good time to break out a jigsaw puzzle, find fun in numbers with sudoku, or paint a picture. You can aim to strengthen your brain’s creative process while not having to worry about what to write for a while. 

•	Declutter your space to declutter your mind. 

Writer’s block can occur when you feel overwhelmed with the clutter of your home and your long list of things to do. Take the time to clean and organize your space, beginning with your work areas. Clear your to-do list of as much as you can to satisfy your brain’s anxiety over having so much to do. 

•	Schedule a time to “meet” your muse. 

Harness your writing muse by scheduling specific times to write. If creativity strikes outside of those specific times, then great – write. If not, then don’t force yourself to come up with words that you don’t have. Stress puts strain on creativity. 

Hopefully, these suggestions will help you overcome writer’s block, or at least inspire you to come up with methods for getting your creativity back. Good luck!  
', 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: Provide some background about "flow" and ways and explanations I can achieve a flow state.
messages:
[{'content': 'Provide some background about "flow" and ways and explanations I can achieve a flow state. ', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': 'Sure! If you've ever gotten so consumed in a task that you forget about the outside world and completely lose track of time, you were likely in a state of flow. It may be commonly referred to as being "in the zone." “Flow” and “flow state” are both terms frequently used in psychology and happiness research. Achieving flow is different than daydreaming, but activates the same part of the brain called the default mode network (DMN). The brain is relaxed when daydreaming, or doing nothing essentially. Interestingly, even though the brain is putting in thoughtful effort in flow, it is enjoyable and relaxing to the brain rather than feeling like work. It actually suppresses anxiety and frees up other parts of the brain to make meaningful connections. 

As the understanding of flow increases, more and more people are looking to see how they can achieve flow. Here are some things you can do to set yourself up to flow: 

1. Set clear goals: First, it’s important to have a defined goal involving the task at hand. A finite goal is more beneficial than a time-oriented goal, as it is more likely to emit a feeling of accomplishment once the goal is met, or the task is finished. 
2. Find things that are the right amount of challenging: If a task or activity is too difficult, it’s hard for the brain to be relaxed enough to be in a flow state. However, the brain needs enough challenge for the brain to see it as interesting and engaging.  
3. Create an environment for focus: This means doing what you need to do to eliminate distractions. This also includes carving out time to achieve flow where you know you won’t be interrupted. 
4. Don’t forget about self-care: Oftentimes in a flow state, people don’t feel thirsty or need to use the bathroom or end up sitting in the same position for a long period that’s not necessarily ergonomic friendly. In order to achieve longer-lasting flow states and take of yourself at the same time, invest the time or energy into getting set up right by doing things like having water readily available or sitting in a proper ergonomic chair. 
5. Put away your phone: This deserves a category in itself because our phones can be the biggest distraction. Turn it off, switch it on do not disturb, or keep it out of sight. Do whatever you need to do to not be tempted to pick up your phone. 
6. Develop a pre-flow ritual: This can involve a number of things like checking your email and messages before tuning in to your work or activity, putting on a designated playlist, doing jumping jacks, etc. It’s more about whatever works for you to clear your mind and set you up for focus. 
7. Get to know yourself: It may take a bit of trial and error to find what works best for you to achieve flow. You can’t enjoy everything, but you can make most things enjoyable by knowing what motivates you and helps you get into a state of flow. 

Psychology experts have determined that flow is associated with increased dopamine, which plays a huge role in regulating mood and motivation. It's also been determined that you can go in and out of flow and have multiple flow states per day, but 90-120 minutes is an optimal flow state for many people. It’s good to want to achieve flow as often as possible in whatever you are doing for overall health and well-being. ', 'role': 'assistant'}]

1. Oil Paint - Oil paint comes in tubes that can be purchased individually or in a set. As you are new to oil painting, a set with basic colors is a good place to start. You will need tubes of white, black, red, blue and yellow.

2. Brushes - As a beginner, you do not need many brushes, it is best to master a few basic sizes before branching out to more costly options. A variety of one or two small, medium, and large round brushes will be enough to begin with. 

3. Turpentine or Mineral Spirits - Oil paint does not require water for brush cleaning. Instead, you use a paint-thinning solution to clean excess paint from the bristles. Turpentine is a commonly used phrase for this substance, but mixtures of odorless mineral spirits are a common alternative. Be sure to work in a well-ventilated area as these liquids can be harmful.

4. A jar for cleaning brushes - You will need a glass vessel with a lid to store your turpentine or mineral spirits for cleaning. Ensure the vessel has a secure lid to seal in the vapor when not used.

5. Linseed Oil or Oil Medium - Much like mineral spirits and turpentine, linseed oil will dilute oil paint.  {'content': 'The way I see it, Zen Buddhism attempts the impossible, and somehow succeeds on occasions. When we were all infants/toddlers, we didn't think very much in words. prompt: Write about the process of making sushi. I want to make sushi and have the ingredients but I have no idea how to make it now.
messages:
[{'content': 'Write about the process of making sushi. I want to make sushi and have the ingredients but I have no idea how to make it now.', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': "There are two ways to roll your maki sushi. One is the traditional maki sushi with nori on the outside, and the other is an inside-out uramaki sushi with rice on the outside. For both, you will first need to prepare your sushi rice and all the ingredients you want to put in your sushi. You will also need a bamboo sushi rolling mat.

To make traditional maki sushi:
1. Place a sheet of nori on the bamboo sushi rolling mat with the rough side facing up.
2. Add a cup of prepared sushi rice and spread it out over the nori sheet using a rice paddle, spoon, or spatula. At the end, wet your fingers in a bowl of water and spread the rice to the very edges with your fingertips. At the edge furthest away from you, leave about 1cm of space so you can seal the sushi at the end.
3. Add your fillings at the end that is closest to you in horizontal rows.
4. Start at the edge that is closest to you and lift the edge of the mat to cover the fillings. Begin slowly rolling the sushi, squeezing gently and tightening the roll as it forms to compress the rice.
5. Slice into eight pieces and serve.

To make the inside-out uramaki:
1. Place a sheet of nori on the bamboo sushi rolling mat with the rough side facing up.
2. Add a cup of prepared sushi rice and spread it out over the nori sheet using a rice paddle, spoon, or spatula. At the end, wet your fingers in a bowl of water and spread the rice to the very edges with your fingertips. This time don't leave any empty space, and spread the rice to all the edges.
3. Flip the nori sheet with the rice onto plastic wrap and place it onto the rolling mat. Add your fillings to the flipped nori sheet at the end that is closest to you in horizontal rows.
4. Start at the edge that is closest to you and lift the edge of the mat to cover the fillings. Begin slowly rolling the sushi, squeezing gently as the roll forms. No need to seal it at the end because the rice will make the roll stick together.
5. Slice into eight pieces and serve.", 'role': 'assistant'}]

1. Add a “sunny side up” egg to a bowl of grits. 

When you have a heaping helping of grits in the mornings, put an over-easy egg on top. Then break the yolk and mix it around until bits of runny yolk and cooked egg whites are dispersed throughout the grits. The richness of the egg yolks combined with the buttery goodness of the grits will give your tastebuds an oomph of flavor and satisfying texture.

2. Deviled eggs are quick, yummy on-the-go foods. 

To make deviled eggs, you boil whole eggs, peel them, and cut them in half, then scoop out the semi-solid yolks. Mix the yolks with mayonnaise, salt, pepper, sweet pickle relish, and a hint of yellow mustard. Then spoon the yolk mixture back into the center of each egg half. Sprinkle with paprika and voila – a delicious, nutritious, more flavorful way to eat eggs!

3. Poach an egg and put it over an English muffin with hollandaise sauce. 

This method of eating eggs is called Eggs Benedict and it’s a savory way to enjoy a hearty breakfast. 

Using water and a tablespoon of vinegar, crack an egg into the liquid and allow it to boil for 3 minutes, then scoop the egg out of the water with a slotted spoon. You can then place it on top of a toasted half of an English muffin with a spoonful of hollandaise sauce. To increase the flavor, you could also add smoked salmon between the egg and muffin before you spoon on the sauce. 

4. Toast, avocado, and eggs – simple, easy, and delicious. 

Sometimes the best, most fulfilling breakfast is the simplest and easiest to prepare. Toast a couple of slices of bread to your liking and add sliced avocado on top. There are two types of estoppel: (1) promissory estoppel and (2) proprietary estoppel. Promissory estoppel arises when a party makes a promise to another party, and that promise is relied upon by the other party to their detriment. Proprietary estoppel, on the other hand, arises when a party has acted to their detriment based on a belief or expectation that they have a certain right or interest in a property.

For example, if a party makes a promise to another party, but the promise is not supported by consideration, the promise may not be legally enforceable. However, if the other party has relied on the promise to their detriment, the principle of promissory estoppel may prevent the party who made the promise from denying it.

For example, in property law, the principle of proprietary estoppel may prevent a landowner from denying that someone else has a right or interest in their land if that person has acted to their detriment based on that belief or expectation.

- Tolerances: No production method is 100% perfect and prototypes are notorious for having less-than-exact dimensions. Decide what tolerances are acceptable for the final product and also what are acceptable for your prototypes.
- Materials: Sometimes a prototype is made in a different material than the final product. 3D printers, in particular, have some distinct material limitations. If your prototype is made of a different material than your end product, research the different effects those materials might give you. 
- Functionality: Does your prototype need to contain all the functions of the final product or is it mainly there to test fit and aesthetics? The latter may be far cheaper to make, but won’t cover all development programs.
- Intellectual property rights: Before you dive deep into the design process, you need to thoroughly research any similar items. There’s no sense in producing even a prototype if the finished product would violate trademarks or patents. Intellectual property lawyers can be very helpful in this regard.

It’s even worse when by estimating anticipated workloads at the service center, managers end up over or under-scheduling the employees. This can lead to both employee and client dissatisfaction.

Naturally, there is optimal scheduling of employees at the service center, ensuring that the right number of employees handle the right amount of work at all times. 

Advancements in machine learning, computer modeling, and predictive and prescriptive analysis in big data present managers with smarter, more streamlined, and forward-looking approaches to employee scheduling – to replace the traditional, ineffective WFM models. 2. Cut out the excess carbs - carbohydrates (rice, sugar, sweets) are okay in moderation, but eating more than a candy bar a day will put extra sugar into your system that your body will not be able to burn off. prompt: Getting your car started can sometimes be a big issue, and I want you to write a list that covers the different reasons that could be causing starting problems. It can be a battery failure, a bad alternator, or a malfunctioning starter motor. Discuss them all briefly. Include a title and a very brief introduction
messages:
[{'content': 'Getting your car started can sometimes be a big issue, and I want you to write a list that covers the different reasons that could be causing starting problems. It can be a battery failure, a bad alternator, or a malfunctioning starter motor. Discuss them all briefly. Include a title and a very brief introduction', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': "Here’s Why Your Vehicle is on Strike 

Doesn't it always ruin your mood when your car just wouldn't start after you last parked it? Here are some common reasons why this could be happening:

1. Alternator Troubles: If you hear a clicking noise instead of a roar, your alternator could be out of commission. The alternator is what charges your battery and powers your car's electrical system. If it's bad, your battery won't maintain a charge, causing your car to stall. 

2. Ignition Apocalypse: Are you turning the key, but getting no response? Your ignition switch may be the culprit. It's responsible for supplying power to your car's electrical system when you turn the key. If it's not working properly, your car won't start. 

3. Battery Blues: If you’re using four years old and never replaced it or you left your headlights on, you might find yourself with a dead battery. A dead battery won't give enough power to crank the engine, rendering your car useless. When it’s new, parking your car for like two weeks in a go can also kill the battery.

4. Timing Belt Issues: The timing belt regulates the movement of valves and pistons in your engine. If it breaks, it can ruin your engine and leave your car unable to start. Keep track of your car's manufacturer recommendations for when to change your timing belt to avoid this issue.

5. Damaged Distributor Cap: The engine's distributor cap is responsible for sending electricity from the ignition coils to the spark plugs. When the cap fails, the spark doesn't reach the right place, and the engine fails to start.

6. Trapped Steering Lock: If the steering wheel is locked due to incorrect usage, the ignition won't turn on, and the car won't start. It could also lead to a broken key or ignition barrel.

7. Sluggish Spark Plugs: Worn, fouled, or corroded spark plugs can lead to poor combustion, affecting engine performance. When they struggle to ignite the air-fuel mixture, the engine might refuse to start at all.

8. Stubborn Starter Motor: A malfunctioning starter motor can make clicking noises or have no response when you try to turn the key. The damage could be due to a dead battery, corroded wires, or a worn-out armature.", 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: Hi, can you tell me about why treelines exist? My friend who lives in the mountains says trees just don’t grow above a certain altitude. Is that true? What makes it happen?
messages:
[{'content': 'Hi, can you tell me about why treelines exist? My friend who lives in the mountains says trees just don’t grow above a certain altitude. Is that true? What makes it happen?', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': "A tree line marks the edge of the conditions in which trees are reliably capable of growing. This is often a function of elevation, but it is more specifically defined by temperature, snowpack, wind, and/or available moisture. In mountainous regions that are tall enough to maintain permanent snowpack, the tree line usually occurs between 300 and 1000 meters below the permanent snow and runs roughly parallel to it.

In most cases, the tree line is defined by the mean seasonal temperature. Even conifer trees will cease to grow where the seasonal mean temperature is less than 6 degrees Celsius (43 Fahrenheit). They need roughly 94 days’ worth of growth time above that temperature to grow successfully.

Some regions of Earth are close enough to the poles that they don’t spend enough time at a growth-sustaining temperature even at sea-level elevations. These regions (the tundra and Antarctic, for example) can be considered to be above the tree line as well.

Other factors can create tree lines, too. Wind can prevent seedlings from growing to a mature height and thus preclude the growth of forests. Some windy areas (especially along coastlines) get stripped of usable soil, so they can’t support tree growth. If there's too little precipitation that will keep trees from growing as well.

Human activities like logging create artificial tree lines, though these lines are not permanent. The only persistent anthropogenic (human-caused) tree line changes come through the effects of climate change.
", 'role': 'assistant'}]

 {'content': "Sure thing! Here is a brief overview of the different types of video games available to play:

1. Role-Playing Games (RPG) - Role-playing games involve playing a fictional character (you can design an avatar of yourself to play in the game) in a certain setting (fantasy, dungeon, wasteland) and playing out a storyline that can organically evolve. The hallmarks of RPGs include an experience-based leveling system, equipment (weapons, armor) that can add attributes (faster running, increased resistance to damage), and quests (tasks that can be completed for experience, equipment, or in-game currency.)
2. First-Person Shooters (FPS) - First-person shooters are shooting games that put you directly in the game character's shoes as if you were seeing everything through their eyes. FPS games usually revolve around either a single-player campaign where the player fights against enemies using a variety of guns through multiple levels, or in multiplayer online matches with other human players (Deathmatch, King-of-the-Hill, Capture-the-Flag, or Cooperative play).
3. Fighting Games - Fighting games are games that usually involve two players (either a human against a computer-controlled character or a human versus another human) fighting against each other using many different fighting techniques, including hand-to-hand combat, weapons combat, and sometimes even superpowers such as laser beams or energy blasts. The winner of the match is the player left standing.
4. Sports Games - Sports games are digital representations of sports that are available in real life (basketball, football, hockey). Sports games allow you to play as a player in a sports game, playing the game as it would be played in real life. Some of these games are made so well that every detail seems almost life-like, and may include real players from the real sports making cameos in the games as playable characters.
5. Side Scroller/Platform Games - Side scroller and platform games are 2-dimensional games where the player controls a character who moves from left to right or vice-versa on the screen and must navigate obstacles such as walls or ladders through jumping (via platforms) or climbing. 
6. Multiplayer Online Battle Arena Games (MOBA) - MOBAs are games that are played online against multiple other human players in a game setting. The games usually consist of groups of players on separate teams attempting to beat each other either by eliminating the opposing team's players or by capturing an objective (such as a flag or castle). The difference between MOBAs and first-person shooters may seem small, but MOBAs do have added features such as different skills for players that can add new dimensions to the game and foster cooperation and communication between teammates to win a match.
7. Action-Adventure Games - Action-adventure games usually involve playing a character in a situation that involves action and/or adventure, such as exploring caves or climbing mountains.
8. Stealth Games - Stealth games require cunning and quiet to kill enemies and maneuver through the game environment. Many stealth games are based around characters that would require stealth to perform their duties, such as ninjas and assassins.
9. Survival Games - Survival games are about playing a character who must survive in their surroundings or the environment. Game modes include surviving against multiple hordes of enemies such as zombies or other enemy combatants using weapons or tools designed to hurt or kill your enemies.
10. Simulation Games - Simulation games allow you to simulate fictional or real-life scenarios in a game setting. Some examples of simulation games include simulating real life (owning a house, interacting with neighbors, making meals), being a farmer (operating a tractor, tending to the land, growing crops), or even pressure-washing dirty fences. There are many simulation games to choose from.", 'role': 'assistant'}]

 {'content': "1 yeast packet
1 teaspoon of salt
1 teaspoon of sugar
2 tablespoons of vegetable oil
Tomato Passata
Cheese
400 grams of flour

Step 1: Preheat the oven to around 200°C-220°C.

Step 2: Weigh out the flour in a bowl on a scale, then add the yeast, sugar, and salt and mix them well. 

Step 3: Make a hole in the centre of the mixture, then add 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil.

Step 4: Add a quarter of a cup of water into the hole, and then mix it into the mixture to create dough.

Step 5: Sprinkle flour liberally onto a surface and then tip the dough out onto it. Roll the dough in the flour and then knead it for a minute, or until it is smooth.

Step 6: Leave the dough to rise under a bowl for 10-15 minutes.

Step 7: Separate the dough into two equal balls, set one in the refrigerator.

Step 8: Start squishing the dough into a pizza shape, cupping your fingers to make the edge more round, and pushing down with your palm to compress it into shape. When the dough is thin enough you can pick it up and spin it in your hands to stretch it out.

Step 9: Once in shape, transfer the dough onto a baking tray lined with parchment paper.

Step 10: Using a spoon, spread the tomato passata out on the dough. Then, grate the cheese and sprinkle it on top of the passata. Use enough cheese to cover the passata, but don't use too much to avoid the pizza becoming soggy.

Step 11: Put the pizza onto the middle shelf of the oven, then set a timer for 15 minutes.

 {'content': 'There are dozens of reasons why an old house may smell a little musty, especially if it has been closed off for a few months, or even years. To get your new home smelling fresh again, follow the ensuing five tips for getting rid of “old house” smells. 

1. Open the windows immediately in every room to completely air out your house. 

The number one cause of musty “old home” smells is stale air. Open every window in your home as often and for as long as you can to encourage the circulation of fresh air. It may take a few days, or even weeks, to fully replace musty smells with fresher, better air throughout your home, so be patient. 

2. Place a dehumidifier in key locations throughout your home and keep them running all the time. 

One large dehumidifier can cover 3,000 square feet of space, so do the math of your new house and calculate how many you would need to cleanse the air of an entire home. Need two? Put one at one end of the house and one at the other, then keep them running continuously until you can smell and feel a positive, cleaner difference in the air. 

3. Cultivate a garden of houseplants that naturally cleanse the air. 

Some plants can naturally reduce indoor air pollutants by replacing musty smells with clean oxygen and earthy, leafy odors. Some air-cleansing houseplants to consider for your indoor garden include: 

•	English Ivy. 
•	Chinese Evergreen. 
•	Dragon Tree. 
•	Pot Mum. 
•	Spider Plants. 
•	Lemon Button Ferns. 
•	Aloe Vera

4. Use small bags of activated charcoal to get rid of musty odors in old drawers, closets, and other walk-in spaces, like attics or basements. 

Did you know that one teaspoon of activated charcoal could dispel bad smells from an entire football field? One teaspoon of activated charcoal lasts for one month. However, for a particularly musty or foul-smelling house, you can change out activated charcoal bags every two weeks. 

The baggies of activated charcoal should be fabric to allow for better, quicker absorbency of bad odors. Or you could simply place a small bowl of activated charcoal in each room but keep it away from pets and children to avoid accidental ingestion. 

5. Burn a combination of your favorite air-cleansing herbs and woods, such as sage, rosemary, and cedar. 

For centuries, the act of burning herbs and wood in an old house has been a method of dispelling negative energies to make way for new beginnings. However, regardless of what you believe in terms of spiritual enlightenment, some herbs, and wood, like sage, rosemary, and cedar, can help eliminate certain allergens and smells, like mold, dust, and pet dander. 

Will it bless your home? Maybe. 
Will it bless your sinuses and help cleanse the air in your home? There’s a good chance! 

Bonus: Sage, rosemary, and cedar are uplifting fragrances, so there’s a chance that your mood will improve as the quality of the air in your home does. ', 'role': 'assistant'}]

2. Taking responsibility - Good leaders take responsibility for the bad choices they make, and the results (or consequences) of those actions. 5. Asking instead of ordering - Good leaders tend to instill trust and confidence in their subordinates. One way they achieve this is by asking subordinates to do tasks, rather than ordering them to do tasks. prompt: I'm in the market for a new home but I'm a first-time buyer. Can you provide me a list of the top 3 things I should look out for when purchasing a home and give some explanations as to why they're important?
messages:
[{'content': "I'm in the market for a new home but I'm a first-time buyer. Can you provide me a list of the top 3 things I should look out for when purchasing a home and give some explanations as to why they're important?", 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': "1. Roof condition - This is an important thing that some first-time buyers may not think about. The first thing you want to know is how old the roof is and what it's made of. Upon learning what the roof is made of, you want to research how long that material lasts and compare that to how old the roof is. This will give you a better idea of how long it has left. Another good thing is to check if the homeowner has a roof certification letter. This letter entails the estimate of the lifespan of the roof typically over the next 2 - 5 years. If you're not confident doing your research, then hiring someone to do a roof inspection would be beneficial. This can often be confused with being bundled into a home inspection, so you want to make sure to hire someone that specializes in diagnosing roof conditions.

2. HVAC condition - It will be good to ask about the type of heating and cooling system the home uses, also be sure to ask how old it is. A typical unit will last somewhere around the timeframe of 10-25 years, hence the importance of asking how old it is. If the unit is missing, shows signs of water damage, has suspicious-looking cracks, or weird sounds and rust, then that's a sign the unit most likely will not be in good working condition. If you still have concerns after checking for those signs then a home inspection would be recommended as they should be more than capable of finding any major issues.

3. Plumbing - For this, there are three main things you need to look for. You'll want to see how fresh the sewer lines are, for example, if the home is 20 or more years old and you don't have any disclosures from the seller it will be beneficial to get a sewer inspection. There are things such as root growth and pipe disintegration that can cause major clogs and mess up the whole system. Next, you want to see how the toilets look. You want to make sure to check for leaks and also unstable bases along with discoloration. Don't be afraid to flush the toilet while you're at the home showing. The same goes for making sure the showers and sinks are working as intended. The final thing you want to check is the state of the water heater. Typically a water heater will last around 10 to 15 years, and when looking at the unit you may find the installation date written on it. If you notice unusual noises when it turns on or notice rust, it is highly recommended to have a professional look at it.", 'role': 'assistant'}]

Article:
What is the Plastic Bag Ban?

As the name states, these bans are bans on single-use plastic bags. Many states around the nation are beginning their bans on plastic bags. These bans will ban all single-use plastic bags, such as the ones that are popularly used at grocery stores and in restaurants for take-out orders.

With these bans in effect, single-use plastic bags will not be accessible for purchase to both shoppers and business owners. As a result, paper bags and reusable cloth bags can be used as an alternative.
	 
Why Should Plastic Bags be Banned?

It’s a fair question. According to different state regulators there are multiple reasons some states are deciding to put these bans in effect, including:

The amount of time it takes plastic bags to decompose
Did you know it can take up to 1,000 years for a plastic bag to decompose?
The damage it can do to our food sources
As plastic breaks down, it makes its way into our water systems—where fish and other sea life consume it, contaminating our food sources with micro-plastics.
The difficulty of recycling them
Plastic bags are very difficult to recycle; and according to the EPA, around 93 billion plastic bags don’t get recycled each year. In 2018, less than 9% of all used plastics were recycled.
The pollution they create, both in the making of plastic bags and in their use
Single-use plastic bags are statistically one of the world’s leading pollutant. A total of 300 million tons of toxic plastic waste is produced every year just in the creation of plastic bags.
Many states across the US are looking to ban plastic bags in an attempt to minimize any future pollution that could be created as a result of plastic bag creation and use.
 Which States are Banning Plastic Bags?

The states that have already banned single-used plastic bags include:

California
Connecticut
Delaware
Hawaii
Maine
New York
Oregon
Vermont
New Jersey

1. Competitive grants: Competitive grants are also known as discretionary funding. The awardee is not chosen beforehand, so the applicant must draft a comprehensive proposal to submit to the review board. Since these are “competitive” grants, there may be multiple organizations and individuals applying for a certain sum of money. 
2. Formula grants: For formula grants, awardees are predetermined. The formula is how grant money is mathematically dispersed among awardees. An example of this type of grant is when state governments are awarded federal funding, but then this allotted amount is broken down into different projects and incentives at the local level. 
3. Continuation grants: As the name implies, these are for grantees that desire to renew an existing grant and continue to receive funding for their projects. It’s important to note that even though the grant money has been awarded in the past, it does not always guarantee continued funding. Those applying for continuation grants will sometimes be competing against those will new ideas and compelling proposals. 
4. Pass-through grants: Pass-through grants are issued by a federal agency, but dealt with by state governments. At the state level, the government has the autonomy to allocate funds where it is deemed necessary in the form of competitive or noncompetitive grants.

prompt: Please provide me with a step-by-step guide on how to make a paper airplane. I will greatly appreciate your assistance.

 {'content': '1. Get an 8.5 x 11 piece of paper, Scotch tape (optional), two hands, and a willingness to keep trying.
2. Fold the paper in half lengthwise and then open it back up.
3. Fold the top corners into the middle crease, creating a triangle at the top of the paper.
4. Fold the point of the triangle down to create another triangle shape.
5. Fold the top corners again, but this time only the corners should meet at the middle crease, forming a little triangle underneath.
6. Fold up the little triangle and crease it tightly to hold the corners down. You can use tape for extra support.
7. Turn the paper airplane over and fold it in half along the middle line.
8. Check your work to make sure the general shape is correct. Start over if needed.
9. Fold down one half of the paper to create the first wing. Adjust the size and crease it about 0.5-1 inch above the bottom of the plane.
10. Turn the airplane over and fold down the other wing to match the first one. Ensure both wings are as equal as possible.
11. Unfold the wings to make them perpendicular to the body of the plane. Check your work, and congratulations on completing a functional paper airplane.
12. For more stability, fold up the very tip of each wing by about a half-inch.
13. You have finished making the paper airplane!', 'role': 'assistant'}]

prompt: Write a Facebook post about setting boundaries at work. It should be 400 words or less. Include three steps for setting boundaries and include examples and actionable tips for how to implement the suggestions.
messages:
[{'content': 'Write a Facebook post about setting boundaries at work. It should be 400 words or less. Include three steps for setting boundaries and include examples and actionable tips for how to implement the suggestions.', 'role': 'user'}
 {'content': 'When was the last time you checked your email after working hours? 
Nodded along silently as a coworker used you as their therapist?
Said yes to a meeting that messed up your schedule? 

If the answer is something like yesterday, it's a sign that you might have a difficult time setting boundaries at work. 

Work-life balance is hard to achieve in today's hustle culture. It can leave us feeling like we have to say yes to everything, constantly go the extra mile, and be everything to everyone just to ensure that our paycheck is secure. 

But that's not true. And actually, doing all those things? Can make you less productive. 

So how can you set boundaries that protect your mental health and your productivity? 

Try these three steps: 

1. Control the narrative. 
Just because someone brings up a subject doesn't mean you have to engage with them. If Sally from Accounting starts talking about her messy divorce the next time you're in the break room, remove yourself from the conversation by saying something like, "Oh, I'm sorry, but there's something I have to do before our break is over." Then take a quick walk outside or call a friend to say hello. The key is to be kind but firm. Once you set this pattern a few times, you'll notice that people will start to remember that you're not up for these types of conversations, and they'll stop trying to engage you in them.

2. Set limits - and stick to them.
What are your non-negotiables? Being home by 6 for dinner? Getting out of the office for lunch? Communicate them to your supervisor in the beginning so they know what to expect. Then hold yourself accountable. Set an alarm that reminds you to wrap things up on time at the end of the day. Make lunch plans, so you have a reason to leave the office.

3. Leave work at work.
Seeing an angry email from a client will ruin your whole weekend. Reading a Slack message from your boss telling you they want to meet on Monday will be the only thing you can think about until you get home from vacation. It's not worth it. You're paid for the time you spend doing your job, not the hours you spend worrying about the weekends.', 'role': 'assistant'}]
